docs.title: pyjelly
docs.text: pyjelly is a Python implementation of Jelly, a high-performance binary serialization format and streaming protocol for RDF knowledge graphs. It works great with RDFLib and also without any extra libraries.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Fast reading and writing of RDF knowledge graphs in the Jelly format
  • SPARQL query results in Jelly-SPARQL
  • Seamless integration with RDFLib
  • Stream processing support for large datasets or streams of many RDF graphs/datasets

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
pyjelly is compatible with Python 3.10 and newer. Python 3.10–3.15 are tested in CI and are guaranteed to work.

The following table shows the compatibility of the pyjelly implementation with other libraries:

pyjelly Python RDFLib Jelly-RDF 0.9.0 – 0.9.0 3.10 – 3.15 7.x (>= 7.1.4) 1.2 0.7.0 – 0.8.2 3.10 – 3.14 7.x (>= 7.1.4) 1.1 0.1.0 – 0.6.2 3.9 – 3.13 7.x (>= 7.1.4) 1.1

See the release notes on GitHub for more details.

docs.title: Commercial and community support
docs.text:
NeverBlink provides commercial support services for Jelly, including implementing custom features, system integrations, implementations for new frameworks, benchmarking, and more.

Community support is available on the Jelly Discord chat.

def parse(self, input_file: IO[bytes]) -> None:
    """
    Read a Jelly stream into the sink.

    The statements, namespaces and identifier of the sink are replaced with
    those read from the stream.

    Args:
        input_file (IO[bytes]): binary file to read.

    """
    from pyjelly.integrations.generic.parse import (  # noqa: PLC0415
        parse_jelly_to_graph,
    )

    parsed_result = parse_jelly_to_graph(input_file)
    self._store = parsed_result._store
    self._namespaces = parsed_result._namespaces
    self._id = parsed_result._id

def serialize(self, output_file: IO[bytes]) -> None:

    Write the sink as a Jelly stream, with the default options.

    To choose the options, use `flat_stream_to_file` or
    `grouped_stream_to_file` from `pyjelly.integrations.generic.serialize`.

    Args:

        grouped_stream_to_file,
    )

    grouped_stream_to_file((sink for sink in [self]), output_file)

def parse_triples_stream(
    frames: Iterable[jelly.RdfStreamFrame],
    options: ParserOptions,
    frame_metadata: ContextVar[MutableMapping[str, bytes]] | None = None,
) -> Generator[Iterable[Triple | Prefix]]:
    """
    Parse flat triple stream.

    Args:
        frames (Iterable[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]): iterator over stream frames
        options (ParserOptions): stream options
        frame_metadata: (ContextVar[ScalarMap[str, bytes]]): context variable
                used for extracting frame metadata

    Yields:
        Generator[Iterable[Triple | Prefix]]:
            Generator of iterables of Triple or Prefix objects,
            one iterable per frame.

    """
    adapter = GenericTriplesAdapter(options)
    decoder = Decoder(adapter=adapter)
    for frame in frames:
        if frame_metadata is not None:
            frame_metadata.set(
                frame.metadata
            ) if frame.metadata else frame_metadata.set({})
        yield decoder.iter_rows(frame)
    if options.params.stream_type == jelly.RDF_STREAM_TYPE_MESSAGES:
        yield decoder.end_of_stream()

def parse_quads_stream(
    frames: Iterable[jelly.RdfStreamFrame],
    options: ParserOptions,
    frame_metadata: ContextVar[MutableMapping[str, bytes]] | None = None,
) -> Generator[Iterable[Quad | Prefix]]:
    """
    Parse flat quads stream.

    Args:
        frames (Iterable[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]): iterator over stream frames
        options (ParserOptions): stream options
        frame_metadata: (ContextVar[ScalarMap[str, bytes]]): context variable
                used for extracting frame metadata

    Yields:
        Generator[Iterable[Quad | Prefix]]:
            Generator of iterables of Quad or Prefix objects,
            one iterable per frame.

    """
    adapter_class: type[GenericQuadsBaseAdapter]
    if options.stream_types.physical_type == jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_QUADS:
        adapter_class = GenericQuadsAdapter
    else:
        adapter_class = GenericGraphsAdapter
    adapter = adapter_class(options=options)
    decoder = Decoder(adapter=adapter)
    for frame in frames:
        if frame_metadata is not None:
            frame_metadata.set(
                frame.metadata
            ) if frame.metadata else frame_metadata.set({})
        yield decoder.iter_rows(frame)
    if options.params.stream_type == jelly.RDF_STREAM_TYPE_MESSAGES:
        yield decoder.end_of_stream()

def parse_jelly_grouped(
    inp: IO[bytes],
    sink_factory: Callable[[], GenericStatementSink] = GenericStatementSink,
    *,
    logical_type_strict: bool = False,
    frame_metadata: ContextVar[MutableMapping[str, bytes]] | None = None,
) -> Generator[GenericStatementSink]:
    """
    Take a jelly file and return generators of generic statements sinks.

    Yields one generic statements sink per frame.

    Args:
        inp (IO[bytes]): input jelly buffered binary stream
        sink_factory (Callable): lambda to construct a statement sink.
            By default, creates an empty in-memory GenericStatementSink.
        logical_type_strict (bool): If True, validate the *logical* type
            in stream options and require a grouped logical type.
            Otherwise, only the physical type is used to route parsing.
        frame_metadata: (ContextVar[ScalarMap[str, bytes]]): context variable
                used for extracting frame metadata

    Raises:
        NotImplementedError: is raised if a physical type is not implemented

    Yields:
        Generator[GenericStatementSink]:
            returns generators for GenericStatementSink, regardless of stream type.

    """
    options, frames = get_options_and_frames(inp)

    st = getattr(options, "stream_types", None)
    if logical_type_strict and (
        st is None
        or st.logical_type == jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED
        or st.flat
    ):
        lt_name = (
            "UNSPECIFIED"
            if st is None
            else jelly.LogicalStreamType.Name(st.logical_type)
        )

        msg = (
            "strict logical type check requires options.stream_types"
            if st is None
            else f"expected GROUPED logical type, got {lt_name}"
        )
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)

    if options.stream_types.physical_type == jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_TRIPLES:
        for graph in grouped_rows(
            parse_triples_stream(
                frames=frames, options=options, frame_metadata=frame_metadata
            ),
            options,
        ):
            sink = sink_factory()
            for graph_item in graph:
                if isinstance(graph_item, Prefix):
                    sink.bind(graph_item.prefix, graph_item.iri)
                else:
                    sink.add(graph_item)
            yield sink
        return
    elif options.stream_types.physical_type in (
        jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_QUADS,
        jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_GRAPHS,
    ):
        for dataset in grouped_rows(
            parse_quads_stream(
                frames=frames, options=options, frame_metadata=frame_metadata
            ),
            options,
        ):
            sink = sink_factory()
            for item in dataset:
                if isinstance(item, Prefix):
                    sink.bind(item.prefix, item.iri)
                else:
                    sink.add(item)
            yield sink
        return

    physical_type_name = jelly.PhysicalStreamType.Name(
        options.stream_types.physical_type
    )
    msg = f"the stream type {physical_type_name} is not supported "
    raise NotImplementedError(msg)

def parse_jelly_to_graph(
    inp: IO[bytes],
    sink_factory: Callable[[], GenericStatementSink] = GenericStatementSink,
) -> GenericStatementSink:
    """
    Add statements from Generator to GenericStatementSink.

    Args:
        inp (IO[bytes]): input jelly stream.
        sink_factory (Callable[[], GenericStatementSink]): factory to create
            statement sink.
            By default creates an empty in-memory GenericStatementSink.
            Has no division for datasets/graphs,
            utilizes the same underlying data structures.

    Returns:
        GenericStatementSink: GenericStatementSink with statements.

    """
    options, frames = get_options_and_frames(inp)
    sink = sink_factory()

    for item in parse_jelly_flat(
        inp=inp, frames=frames, options=options, logical_type_strict=False
    ):
        if isinstance(item, Prefix):
            sink.bind(item.prefix, item.iri)  # type: ignore[union-attr, unused-ignore]
        else:
            sink.add(item)
    return sink

def parse_jelly_flat(
    inp: IO[bytes],
    frames: Iterable[jelly.RdfStreamFrame] | None = None,
    options: ParserOptions | None = None,
    *,
    logical_type_strict: bool = False,
) -> Generator[Statement | Prefix]:  # type: ignore[valid-type, unused-ignore]
    """
    Parse jelly file with FLAT logical type into a Generator of stream events.

    Args:
        inp (IO[bytes]): input jelly buffered binary stream.
        frames (Iterable[jelly.RdfStreamFrame | None):
            jelly frames if read before.
        options (ParserOptions | None): stream options
            if read before.
        logical_type_strict (bool): If True, validate the *logical* type
            in stream options and require FLAT (TRIPLES/QUADS).
            Otherwise, only the physical type is used to route parsing.

    Raises:
        NotImplementedError: if physical type is not supported

    Yields:
        Generator[Statement | Prefix]: Generator of stream events

    """
    if frames is None or options is None:
        options, frames = get_options_and_frames(inp)

    st = getattr(options, "stream_types", None)
    if logical_type_strict and (st is None or not st.flat):
        lt_name = (
            "UNSPECIFIED"
            if st is None
            else jelly.LogicalStreamType.Name(st.logical_type)
        )

        msg = (
            "strict logical type check requires options.stream_types"
            if st is None
            else f"expected FLAT logical type (TRIPLES/QUADS), got {lt_name}"
        )
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)

    if options.stream_types.physical_type == jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_TRIPLES:
        yield from flat_rows(
            parse_triples_stream(frames=frames, options=options), options
        )
        return
    if options.stream_types.physical_type in (
        jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_QUADS,
        jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_GRAPHS,
    ):
        yield from flat_rows(
            parse_quads_stream(frames=frames, options=options), options
        )
        return
    physical_type_name = jelly.PhysicalStreamType.Name(
        options.stream_types.physical_type
    )
    msg = f"the stream type {physical_type_name} is not supported "
    raise NotImplementedError(msg)

    lookup_preset: options.LookupPreset | None = None,

    if lookup_preset is None:
        lookup_preset = options.LookupPreset()

    self.datatypes = LookupEncoder(lookup_size=lookup_preset.max_datatypes)
    # Where rows for new lookup entries go in the row layout. A stream replaces
    # it with its own.
    self.flow: FrameFlow = ManualFrameFlow()
    self.iri_cache: dict[str, _CachedIri] = {}
    # Cleared when full, so that a long stream doesn't grow it without bound
    self.iri_cache_size = max(4 * lookup_preset.max_names, 1024)
    # The encoded subject, predicate, object and graph of the statement
    self.encoded = [EncodedTerm() for _ in range(4)]
    # Set by streams of Jelly-RDF 1.2. Then IRIs are encoded with the indices of
    # their entries, new entries are packed (see PackedEntries), and quoted
    # triples are encoded as triple terms.
    self.column_layout = False
    # The RDF version that a Jelly-RDF 1.2 stream declares, which limits its terms
    self.rdf_version: int = jelly.RDF_VERSION_UNSPECIFIED
    # The IRI sequence of the triple terms of a frame (only the object column can
    # have them): the indices of the last IRI. -1 makes the first IRI state its
    # prefix.
    self.triple_prefix_index = -1
    self.triple_name_index = 0
    # How deep the triple term being encoded is nested, and how many IRIs the
    # outermost one has so far
    self.triple_depth = 0
    self.triple_iris = 0

Check whether two terms are equal, to find repeated terms.

IRIs, blank nodes and literals are compared field by field, which is cheaper than calling their eq.

Source code in pyjelly/integrations/generic/serialize.py 
def same_term(self, a: object, b: object) -> bool:
    """
    Check whether two terms are equal, to find repeated terms.

    IRIs, blank nodes and literals are compared field by field, which is
    cheaper than calling their __eq__.
    """
    if a is b:
        return True
    cls = type(a)
    if cls is not type(b):
        return False
    if cls is IRI:
        return cast(IRI, a)._iri == cast(IRI, b)._iri
    if cls is BlankNode:
        return cast(BlankNode, a)._id == cast(BlankNode, b)._id
    if cls is Literal:
        x = cast(Literal, a)
        y = cast(Literal, b)
        return (
            x._lex == y._lex
            and x._langtag == y._langtag
            and x._datatype == y._datatype
            and x._direction == y._direction
        )
    return a == b

def encode_spo(self, term: object, out: EncodedTerm) -> None:
    """
    Encode term based on its GenericSink object.

    Args:
        term (object): term to encode
        out (EncodedTerm): where to put the encoded term.

    """
    if isinstance(term, IRI):
        self.encode_iri(term._iri, out)
        return

    if isinstance(term, Literal):
        self.encode_literal(
            lex=term._lex,
            language=term._langtag,
            datatype=term._datatype,
            direction=term._direction,
            out=out,
        )
        return

    if isinstance(term, BlankNode):
        self.encode_bnode(term._id, out)
        return

    if isinstance(term, Triple):
        self.encode_quoted_triple(term, out)
        return

    super().encode_spo(term, out)  # raises NotImplementedError

@stream_frames.register(TripleStream)
def triples_stream_frames(
    stream: TripleStream,
    data: GenericStatementSink | Generator[Triple],
) -> Generator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]:
    """
    Serialize a GenericStatementSink into frames using physical type triples stream.

    Args:
        stream (TripleStream): stream that specifies triples processing
        data (GenericStatementSink | Generator[Triple]):
            GenericStatementSink/Statements to serialize.

    Yields:
        Generator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]: jelly frames.

    """
    stream.enroll()
    if (
        isinstance(data, GenericStatementSink)
        and stream.options.params.namespace_declarations
    ):
        yield from namespace_declarations(data, stream)

    graphs = (data,)
    for graph in graphs:
        for terms in graph:
            if frame := stream.triple(terms):
                yield frame
        if frame := stream.flow.frame_from_graph():
            yield frame
    if stream.stream_types.flat and (frame := stream.flow.to_stream_frame()):
        yield frame

def guess_options(
    sink: GenericStatementSink, *, grouped: bool = False
) -> SerializerOptions:
    """
    Guess the serializer options based on the store type.

    For a stream of graphs or datasets (`grouped`), each is an RDF Message in
    Jelly-RDF 1.2, and one frame in Jelly-RDF 1.1.
    """
    if sink.is_triples_sink:
        logical_type = (
            jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_GRAPHS
            if grouped
            else jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_FLAT_TRIPLES
        )
    else:
        logical_type = (
            jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_DATASETS
            if grouped
            else jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_FLAT_QUADS
        )
    # Generic sink supports both RDF-star and generalized statements by default
    # as it can handle any term types including quoted triples and generalized RDF terms
    params = StreamParameters(generalized_statements=True, rdf_star=True)
    return SerializerOptions(logical_type=logical_type, params=params)

def guess_stream(options: SerializerOptions, sink: GenericStatementSink) -> Stream:
    """
    Return an appropriate stream implementation for the given options.

    Notes: if base(!) logical type is GRAPHS and sink.is_triples_sink is false,
        initializes TripleStream
    """
    stream_cls: type[Stream]
    if (
        options.logical_type % 10
    ) != jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_GRAPHS and not sink.is_triples_sink:
        stream_cls = QuadStream
    else:
        stream_cls = TripleStream
    if options is not None:
        lookup_preset = options.lookup_preset
    return stream_cls(
        encoder=GenericSinkTermEncoder(lookup_preset=lookup_preset),
        options=options,
    )

def grouped_stream_to_frames(
    sink_generator: Generator[GenericStatementSink],
    options: SerializerOptions | None = None,
) -> Generator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]:
    """
    Transform multiple GenericStatementSinks into Jelly frames.

    Notes:
        One frame per GenericStatementSink.

    Note: options are guessed if not provided.

    Args:
        sink_generator (Generator[GenericStatementSink]): Generator of
            GenericStatementSink to transform.
        options (SerializerOptions | None, optional): stream options to use.
            Options are guessed based on the sink store type. Defaults to None.

    Yields:
        Generator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]: produced Jelly frames

    """
    stream = None
    for sink in sink_generator:
        if not stream:
            if options is None:
                options = guess_options(sink, grouped=True)
            stream = guess_stream(options, sink)
        yield from stream_frames(stream, sink)

def flat_stream_to_frames(
    statements: Generator[Triple | Quad],
    options: SerializerOptions | None = None,
) -> Generator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]:
    """
    Serialize a stream of raw GenericStatementSink's triples or quads into Jelly frames.

    Args:
        statements (Generator[Triple | Quad]):
          s/p/o triples or s/p/o/g quads to serialize.
        options (SerializerOptions | None, optional):
            if omitted, guessed based on the first tuple.

    Yields:
        Generator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]: generated frames.

    """
    first = next(statements, None)
    if first is None:
        return

    sink = GenericStatementSink()
    sink.add(first)
    if options is None:
        options = guess_options(sink)
    stream = guess_stream(options, sink)

    combined: Generator[Triple | Quad] | GenericStatementSink = (
        item for item in chain([first], statements)
    )

    yield from stream_frames(stream, combined)

def serialize_jelly_sparql_sequence(
    results: Iterable[SequenceItem],
    out: IO[bytes],
    options: SparqlOptions | None = None,
) -> None:
    """
    Write a sequence of SPARQL query results in one Jelly-SPARQL stream.

    The stream is PUNCTUATED, with one result set per result.

    Args:
        results (Iterable[SequenceItem]): the results, each a (variables, rows)
            pair for a SELECT query, or a bool for an ASK query.
        out (IO[bytes]): output stream.
        options (SparqlOptions | None): options of the stream, which must be
            punctuated. Defaults to SparqlOptions(punctuated=True).

    """
    if options is None:
        options = SparqlOptions(punctuated=True)
    if not options.punctuated:
        msg = "a sequence of results needs SparqlOptions(punctuated=True)"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    stream = sparql_stream(options)
    writer = FrameWriter(out, delimited=True)
    for result in results:
        if isinstance(result, bool):
            writer.write(stream.ask(result))
        else:
            variables, rows = result
            write_solutions(stream, variables, rows, writer)

        self.vars = [Variable(name) for name in names]
    return self.vars

def __init__(
    self,
    lookup_preset: options.LookupPreset | None = None,
) -> None:
    if lookup_preset is None:
        lookup_preset = options.LookupPreset()
    self.lookup_preset = lookup_preset
    self.names = LookupEncoder(lookup_size=lookup_preset.max_names)
    self.prefixes = LookupEncoder(lookup_size=lookup_preset.max_prefixes)
    self.datatypes = LookupEncoder(lookup_size=lookup_preset.max_datatypes)
    # Where rows for new lookup entries go in the row layout. A stream replaces
    # it with its own.
    self.flow: FrameFlow = ManualFrameFlow()
    self.iri_cache: dict[str, _CachedIri] = {}
    # Cleared when full, so that a long stream doesn't grow it without bound
    self.iri_cache_size = max(4 * lookup_preset.max_names, 1024)
    # The encoded subject, predicate, object and graph of the statement
    self.encoded = [EncodedTerm() for _ in range(4)]
    # Set by streams of Jelly-RDF 1.2. Then IRIs are encoded with the indices of
    # their entries, new entries are packed (see PackedEntries), and quoted
    # triples are encoded as triple terms.
    self.column_layout = False
    # The RDF version that a Jelly-RDF 1.2 stream declares, which limits its terms
    self.rdf_version: int = jelly.RDF_VERSION_UNSPECIFIED
    # The IRI sequence of the triple terms of a frame (only the object column can
    # have them): the indices of the last IRI. -1 makes the first IRI state its
    # prefix.
    self.triple_prefix_index = -1
    self.triple_name_index = 0
    # How deep the triple term being encoded is nested, and how many IRIs the
    # outermost one has so far
    self.triple_depth = 0
    self.triple_iris = 0
same_term(a, b)

Return whether two terms are equal, for repeated terms.

rdflib's eq is slow Python code, so the common cases are answered here by comparing the terms as strings:

  • Two URIRefs or two BNodes are equal if their strings are.
  • Two Literals with different lexical forms are never equal. With the same lexical form, language tag and datatype, they are equal. Otherwise rdflib decides (e.g., for language tags that differ only in case).
  • Terms of different classes among these three are never equal.
Source code in pyjelly/integrations/rdflib/encode.py 
def same_term(self, a: object, b: object) -> bool:
    """
    Return whether two terms are equal, for repeated terms.

    rdflib's __eq__ is slow Python code, so the common cases are answered here
    by comparing the terms as strings:

    - Two URIRefs or two BNodes are equal if their strings are.
    - Two Literals with different lexical forms are never equal. With the same
      lexical form, language tag and datatype, they are equal. Otherwise rdflib
      decides (e.g., for language tags that differ only in case).
    - Terms of different classes among these three are never equal.
    """
    if a is b:
        return True
    cls = type(a)
    other_cls = type(b)
    if cls is other_cls:
        if cls is URIRef or cls is BNode:
            a_str: str = cast("str", a)
            b_str: str = cast("str", b)
            return a_str == b_str
        if cls is Literal:
            a_lex: str = cast("str", a)
            b_lex: str = cast("str", b)
            if a_lex != b_lex:
                return False
            # Slots behind the language and datatype properties
            a_node: Any = a
            b_node: Any = b
            if _same_str(a_node._language, b_node._language) and _same_str(
                a_node._datatype, b_node._datatype
            ):
                return True
    elif (cls is URIRef or cls is BNode or cls is Literal) and (
        other_cls is URIRef or other_cls is BNode or other_cls is Literal
    ):
        return False
    return a == b

def encode_spo(self, term: object, out: EncodedTerm) -> None:
    """
    Encode s/p/o term based on its RDFLib object.

    Args:
        term (object): term to encode
        out (EncodedTerm): where to put the encoded term.

    """
    # Exact type checks first, as rdflib almost always makes terms of these
    # exact classes: they are cheaper than isinstance(), which is the fallback
    # for subclasses, and runs Python code for rdflib's abstract classes.
    # `node` is Any, because the type checks don't narrow the type when
    # rdflib isn't installed (as during the mypyc compilation).
    node: Any = term
    cls = type(node)
    if cls is URIRef or (
        cls is not Literal and cls is not BNode and isinstance(node, URIRef)
    ):
        # A plain str, so that the IRI cache never calls rdflib's __eq__
        self.encode_iri(str(node), out)
        return

    if cls is Literal or (cls is not BNode and isinstance(node, Literal)):
        # The slots behind the language and datatype properties, which are
        # Python functions
        datatype = node._datatype
        self.encode_literal(
            lex=str(node),
            language=node._language,
            # `datatype` is cast to `str` explicitly because
            # `URIRef.__eq__` overrides `str.__eq__` in an incompatible manner
            datatype=datatype and str(datatype),
            out=out,
        )
        return

    if isinstance(node, BNode):
        self.encode_bnode(str(node), out)
        return

    super().encode_spo(term, out)  # raises NotImplementedError

def encode_graph(self, term: object, out: EncodedTerm) -> None:
    """
    Encode graph name term based on its RDFLib object.

    Args:
        term (object): term to encode
        out (EncodedTerm): where to put the encoded graph name.

    """
    if self.same_term(term, DATASET_DEFAULT_GRAPH_ID):
        self.encode_default_graph(out)
        return

    # Exact type checks first, see encode_spo()
    cls = type(term)
    if cls is URIRef or (cls is not BNode and isinstance(term, URIRef)):
        self.encode_iri(str(term), out)
        return

    if isinstance(term, BNode):
        self.encode_bnode(str(term), out)
        return
    super().encode_graph(term, out)  # raises NotImplementedError

def parse(
    self,
    source: InputSource,
    sink: Graph,
    *,
    validate_iris: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """
    Parse jelly file into provided RDFLib Graph.

    Args:
        source (InputSource): jelly file as buffered binary stream InputSource obj
        sink (Graph): RDFLib Graph
        validate_iris (bool): whether rdflib checks the IRIs, see
            parse_jelly_to_graph(). Pass it to Graph.parse().

    Raises:
        TypeError: raises error if invalid input

    """
    byte_stream = source.getByteStream()
    if byte_stream is None:
        msg = "expected source to be a stream of bytes"
        raise TypeError(msg)

    inp = cast(IO[bytes], byte_stream)
    if inp is None:
        msg = "expected source to be a stream of bytes"
        raise TypeError(msg)
    # The default graph of a stream of quads goes into the Graph that rdflib
    # parses into, as with TriG and N-Quads: for Dataset.parse(), that is the
    # Dataset's default graph
    target = Graph(store=sink.store, identifier=sink.identifier)
    parse_jelly_to_graph(
        inp,
        graph_factory=lambda: target,
        dataset_factory=lambda: Dataset(store=sink.store),
        validate_iris=validate_iris,
        default_graph=target,
    )

def parse_triples_stream(
    frames: Iterable[jelly.RdfStreamFrame],
    options: ParserOptions,
    frame_metadata: ContextVar[MutableMapping[str, bytes]] | None = None,
    *,
    validate_iris: bool = False,
) -> Generator[Iterable[Triple | Prefix]]:
    """
    Parse flat triple stream.

    Args:
        frames (Iterable[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]): iterator over stream frames
        options (ParserOptions): stream options
        frame_metadata: (ContextVar[ScalarMap[str, bytes]]): context variable
            used for extracting frame metadata
        validate_iris (bool): whether rdflib checks the IRIs. An invalid IRI is
            still read, rdflib only logs a warning. Checking slows down parsing.

    Yields:
        Generator[Iterable[Triple | Prefix]]:
            Generator of iterables of Triple or Prefix objects,
            one iterable per frame.

    """
    adapter = RDFLibTriplesAdapter(options, validate_iris=validate_iris)
    decoder = Decoder(adapter=adapter)
    for frame in frames:
        if frame_metadata is not None:
            frame_metadata.set(
                frame.metadata
            ) if frame.metadata else frame_metadata.set({})
        yield decoder.iter_rows(frame)
    if options.params.stream_type == jelly.RDF_STREAM_TYPE_MESSAGES:
        yield decoder.end_of_stream()

def parse_jelly_grouped(  # noqa: PLR0913 keyword-only options
    inp: IO[bytes],
    graph_factory: Callable[[], Graph] = Graph,
    dataset_factory: Callable[[], Dataset] = Dataset,
    *,
    logical_type_strict: bool = False,
    frame_metadata: ContextVar[MutableMapping[str, bytes]] | None = None,
    validate_iris: bool = False,
) -> Generator[Graph] | Generator[Dataset]:
    """
    Take jelly file and return generators based on the detected physical type.

    Yields one graph/dataset per frame.

    Args:
        inp (IO[bytes]): input jelly buffered binary stream
        graph_factory (Callable): lambda to construct a Graph.
            By default creates an empty in-memory Graph,
            but you can pass something else here.
        dataset_factory (Callable): lambda to construct a Dataset.
            By default creates an empty in-memory Dataset,
            but you can pass something else here.
        logical_type_strict (bool): If True, validate the *logical* type in
            stream options and require a grouped logical type. Otherwise, only the
            physical type is used to route parsing.
        frame_metadata: (ContextVar[ScalarMap[str, bytes]]): context variable
            used for extracting frame metadata
        validate_iris (bool): whether rdflib checks the IRIs. An invalid IRI is
            still read, rdflib only logs a warning. Checking slows down parsing.

    Raises:
        NotImplementedError: is raised if a physical type is not implemented

    Yields:
        Generator[Graph] | Generator[Dataset]:
            returns generators for graphs/datasets based on the type of input

    """
    options, frames = get_options_and_frames(inp)

    st = getattr(options, "stream_types", None)
    if logical_type_strict and (
        st is None
        or st.logical_type == jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED
        or st.flat
    ):
        lt_name = (
            "UNSPECIFIED"
            if st is None
            else jelly.LogicalStreamType.Name(st.logical_type)
        )

        msg = (
            "strict logical type check requires options.stream_types"
            if st is None
            else f"expected GROUPED logical type, got {lt_name}"
        )
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)

    if options.stream_types.physical_type == jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_TRIPLES:
        for graph in grouped_rows(
            parse_triples_stream(
                frames=frames,
                options=options,
                frame_metadata=frame_metadata,
                validate_iris=validate_iris,
            ),
            options,
        ):
            sink = graph_factory()
            for graph_item in graph:
                if isinstance(graph_item, Prefix):
                    sink.bind(graph_item.prefix, graph_item.iri)
                else:
                    sink.add(graph_item)
            yield sink
        return
    elif options.stream_types.physical_type in (
        jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_QUADS,
        jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_GRAPHS,
    ):
        for dataset in grouped_rows(
            parse_quads_stream(
                frames=frames,
                options=options,
                frame_metadata=frame_metadata,
                validate_iris=validate_iris,
            ),
            options,
        ):
            sink = dataset_factory()
            for item in dataset:
                if isinstance(item, Prefix):
                    sink.bind(item.prefix, item.iri)
                else:
                    s, p, o, graph_name = item
                    context = sink.get_context(graph_name)
                    sink.add((s, p, o, context))
            yield sink
        return

    physical_type_name = jelly.PhysicalStreamType.Name(
        options.stream_types.physical_type
    )
    msg = f"the stream type {physical_type_name} is not supported "
    raise NotImplementedError(msg)

def parse_jelly_to_graph(
    inp: IO[bytes],
    graph_factory: Callable[[], Graph] = Graph,
    dataset_factory: Callable[[], Dataset] = Dataset,
    *,
    validate_iris: bool = False,
    default_graph: Graph | None = None,
) -> Graph | Dataset:
    """
    Add statements from Generator to provided Graph/Dataset.

    Args:
        inp (IO[bytes]): input jelly stream.
        graph_factory (Callable[[], Graph]): factory to create Graph.
            By default creates an empty in-memory Graph,
            but you can pass something else here.
        dataset_factory (Callable[[], Dataset]): factory to create Dataset.
            By default creates an empty in-memory Dataset,
            but you can pass something else here.
        validate_iris (bool): whether rdflib checks the IRIs. An invalid IRI is
            still read, rdflib only logs a warning. Checking slows down parsing.
        default_graph (Graph | None): graph for the quads in the default graph,
            in the same store as the Dataset. By default, the Dataset's default
            graph.

    Returns:
        Dataset | Graph: Dataset or Graph with statements.

    """
    options, frames = get_options_and_frames(inp)

    sink: Graph
    if options.stream_types.physical_type == jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_TRIPLES:
        sink = graph_factory()
        # Graph.add only checks the terms before giving them to the store
        to_store = type(sink).add is Graph.add
    else:
        # Other stream types fail in parse_jelly_flat
        sink = dataset_factory()
        # Dataset.add would also make a new context graph for every quad
        to_store = type(sink).add is ConjunctiveGraph.add

    items = parse_jelly_flat(
        inp=inp, frames=frames, options=options, validate_iris=validate_iris
    )
    if to_store:
        _add_to_store(sink, items, default_graph)
        return sink

    # The Graph or Dataset class changes add(), so it gets every statement
    for item in items:
        if isinstance(item, Prefix):
            sink.bind(item.prefix, item.iri)
        if isinstance(item, Triple):
            sink.add(item)
        if isinstance(item, Quad):
            s, p, o, graph_name = item
            if default_graph is not None and graph_name == DATASET_DEFAULT_GRAPH_ID:
                context = default_graph
            else:
                context = cast(Dataset, sink).get_context(graph_name)
            sink.add((s, p, o, context))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    return sink

def parse_jelly_flat(
    inp: IO[bytes],
    frames: Iterable[jelly.RdfStreamFrame] | None = None,
    options: ParserOptions | None = None,
    *,
    logical_type_strict: bool = False,
    validate_iris: bool = False,
) -> Generator[Statement | Prefix]:
    """
    Parse jelly file with FLAT logical type into a Generator of stream events.

    Args:
        inp (IO[bytes]): input jelly buffered binary stream.
        frames (Iterable[jelly.RdfStreamFrame | None):
            jelly frames if read before.
        options (ParserOptions | None): stream options
            if read before.
        logical_type_strict (bool): If True, validate the *logical* type in
            stream options and require FLAT_(TRIPLES|QUADS). Otherwise, only the
            physical type is used to route parsing.
        validate_iris (bool): whether rdflib checks the IRIs. An invalid IRI is
            still read, rdflib only logs a warning. Checking slows down parsing.

    Raises:
        NotImplementedError: if physical type is not supported

    Yields:
        Generator[Statement | Prefix]: Generator of stream events

    """
    if frames is None or options is None:
        options, frames = get_options_and_frames(inp)

    st = getattr(options, "stream_types", None)
    if logical_type_strict and (st is None or not st.flat):
        lt_name = (
            "UNSPECIFIED"
            if st is None
            else jelly.LogicalStreamType.Name(st.logical_type)
        )
        msg = (
            "strict logical type check requires options.stream_types"
            if st is None
            else f"expected FLAT logical type (TRIPLES/QUADS), got {lt_name}"
        )
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)

    if options.stream_types.physical_type == jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_TRIPLES:
        yield from flat_rows(
            parse_triples_stream(
                frames=frames, options=options, validate_iris=validate_iris
            ),
            options,
        )
        return
    if options.stream_types.physical_type in (
        jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_QUADS,
        jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_GRAPHS,
    ):
        yield from flat_rows(
            parse_quads_stream(frames=frames, options=options), options
        )
        return
    physical_type_name = jelly.PhysicalStreamType.Name(
        options.stream_types.physical_type
    )
    msg = f"the stream type {physical_type_name} is not supported "
    raise NotImplementedError(msg)

def serialize(  # type: ignore[override]
    self,
    out: IO[bytes],
    /,
    *,
    stream: Stream | None = None,
    options: SerializerOptions | None = None,
    **unused: Any,
) -> None:
    """
    Serialize self.store content to Jelly format.

    Args:
        out (IO[bytes]): output buffered writer
        stream (Stream | None, optional): Jelly stream object. Defaults to None.
        options (SerializerOptions | None, optional): Serializer options
            if defined beforehand, e.g., read from a separate file.
            Defaults to None.
        **unused(Any): unused args for RDFLib serialize

    """
    if options is None:
        options = guess_options(self.store)
    if stream is None:
        stream = guess_stream(options, self.store)
    frames = stream_frames(stream, self.store)
    if stream.options.params.delimited:
        for stream_frame in frames:
            write_delimited(stream_frame, out)
        return
    written = False
    for stream_frame in frames:
        if written:
            msg = (
                "the data does not fit in one frame. A non-delimited stream can "
                "only have one frame. Write a delimited stream, or use larger "
                "lookups."
            )
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        write_single(stream_frame, out)
        written = True

@stream_frames.register(TripleStream)
def triples_stream_frames(
    stream: TripleStream,
    data: Graph | Dataset | Iterable[Triple],
) -> Generator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]:
    """
    Serialize a Graph/Dataset into jelly frames.

    Args:
        stream (TripleStream): stream that specifies triples processing
        data (Graph | Dataset | Iterable[Triple]):
            Graph/Dataset/Statements to serialize.

    Notes:
        if Dataset (or ConjunctiveGraph) is given, its graphs are unpacked and
        iterated over. If flow is GraphsFrameFlow, emits a frame per graph.

    Yields:
        Generator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]: jelly frames.

    """
    stream.enroll()
    if isinstance(data, Graph) and stream.options.params.namespace_declarations:
        yield from namespace_declarations(data, stream)

    graphs: Iterable[Graph | Iterable[Triple]]
    if isinstance(data, Dataset):
        graphs = data.graphs()
    elif isinstance(data, ConjunctiveGraph):
        graphs = data.contexts()
    else:
        graphs = (data,)
    for graph in graphs:
        tree = spo_tree(graph) if isinstance(graph, Graph) else None
        if tree is not None:
            # An in-memory graph, grouped by subject and predicate
            yield from write_tree(stream, tree)
        else:
            # Any other store, or a generator of triples, in its own order
            yield from stream.triples(graph)
        if frame := stream.flow.frame_from_graph():
            yield frame
    if stream.stream_types.flat and (frame := stream.flow.to_stream_frame()):
        yield frame

    stream: QuadStream,
    data: Dataset | Iterable[Quad],

    Serialize a Dataset into jelly frames.

        Emits one frame per dataset if flow is of DatasetsFrameFlow.
        A ConjunctiveGraph is written as a Dataset, with its default context
        as the default graph.

        stream (QuadStream): stream that specifies quads processing
        data (Dataset | Iterable[Quad]): Dataset to serialize.

        # An in-memory dataset, grouped by graph, subject and predicate

    else:

        quads = dataset_quads(data) if isinstance(data, ConjunctiveGraph) else data

def guess_options(sink: Graph | Dataset, *, grouped: bool = False) -> SerializerOptions:
    """
    Guess the serializer options based on the store type.

    For a stream of graphs or datasets (`grouped`), each is an RDF Message in
    Jelly-RDF 1.2, and one frame in Jelly-RDF 1.1.

    >>> guess_options(Graph()).logical_type
    1
    >>> guess_options(Dataset()).logical_type
    2
    >>> guess_options(Dataset(), grouped=True).logical_type
    4

    A ConjunctiveGraph (e.g., the one rdfpipe reads into) holds quads too:

    >>> guess_options(ConjunctiveGraph()).logical_type
    2
    """
    if isinstance(sink, ConjunctiveGraph):
        logical_type = (
            jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_DATASETS
            if grouped
            else jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_FLAT_QUADS
        )
    else:
        logical_type = (
            jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_GRAPHS
            if grouped
            else jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_FLAT_TRIPLES
        )
    # RDFLib doesn't support RDF-star and generalized statements by default
    # as it requires specific handling for quoted triples and non-standard RDF terms
    params = StreamParameters(generalized_statements=False, rdf_star=False)
    return SerializerOptions(logical_type=logical_type, params=params)

def guess_stream(options: SerializerOptions, sink: Graph | Dataset) -> Stream:
    """
    Return an appropriate stream implementation for the given options.

    Notes: if base(!) logical type is GRAPHS and Dataset (or ConjunctiveGraph)
        is given, initializes TripleStream

    >>> graph_ser = RDFLibJellySerializer(Graph())
    >>> ds_ser = RDFLibJellySerializer(Dataset())

    >>> type(guess_stream(guess_options(graph_ser.store), graph_ser.store))
    <class 'pyjelly.serialize.streams.TripleStream'>
    >>> type(guess_stream(guess_options(ds_ser.store), ds_ser.store))
    <class 'pyjelly.serialize.streams.QuadStream'>
    """
    stream_cls: type[Stream]
    if (options.logical_type % 10) != jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_GRAPHS and isinstance(
        sink, ConjunctiveGraph
    ):
        stream_cls = QuadStream
    else:
        stream_cls = TripleStream
    return stream_cls.for_rdflib(options=options)

def grouped_stream_to_frames(
    sink_generator: Generator[Graph] | Generator[Dataset],
    options: SerializerOptions | None = None,
) -> Generator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]:
    """
    Transform Graphs/Datasets into Jelly frames, one frame per Graph/Dataset.

    Note: options are guessed if not provided.

    Args:
        sink_generator (Generator[Graph] | Generator[Dataset]): Generator of
            Graphs/Dataset to transform.
        options (SerializerOptions | None, optional): stream options to use.
            Options are guessed based on the sink store type. Defaults to None.

    Yields:
        Generator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]: produced Jelly frames

    """
    stream = None
    for sink in sink_generator:
        if not stream:
            if options is None:
                options = guess_options(sink, grouped=True)
            stream = guess_stream(options, sink)
        yield from stream_frames(stream, sink)

def flat_stream_to_frames(
    statements: Generator[Triple | Quad],
    options: SerializerOptions | None = None,
) -> Generator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]:
    """
    Serialize a stream of raw triples or quads into Jelly frames.

    Args:
        statements (Generator[Triple | Quad]):
          s/p/o triples or s/p/o/g quads to serialize.
        options (SerializerOptions | None, optional):
            if omitted, guessed based on the first tuple.

    Yields:
        Generator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]: generated frames.

    """
    first = next(statements, None)
    if first is None:
        return

    sink = Dataset() if len(first) == QUAD_ARITY else Graph()
    if options is None:
        options = guess_options(sink)
    stream = guess_stream(options, sink)

    yield from stream_frames(stream, chain([first], statements))

@override
def parse(  # type: ignore[override]
    self,
    source: IO[bytes] | bytes | str | Path,
    content_type: str | None = None,
    *,
    validate_iris: bool = False,
    lazy: bool = False,
) -> Result:
    """
    Read the results.

    Args:
        source (IO[bytes] | bytes | str | Path): a stream, bytes, or a file
            path.
        content_type (str | None): unused.
        validate_iris (bool): whether rdflib checks the IRIs, see
            parse_jelly_sparql().
        lazy (bool): read the rows during iteration, see parse_jelly_sparql().
            Only for streams, not paths.

    """
    if not isinstance(source, (str, Path)):
        return parse_jelly_sparql(source, validate_iris=validate_iris, lazy=lazy)
    if lazy:
        msg = "lazy reading needs a stream that stays open, not a path"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    with Path(source).open("rb") as inp:
        return parse_jelly_sparql(inp, validate_iris=validate_iris)

Args: inp (IO[bytes] | bytes): the stream, delimited or not. It must have one result set (the FLAT stream type, the default). validate_iris (bool): whether rdflib checks the IRIs. def parse_jelly_sparql(
    inp: IO[bytes] | bytes, *, validate_iris: bool = False, lazy: bool = False
) -> JellySparqlResult:
    """
    Read SPARQL query results from Jelly-SPARQL.

    Args:
        inp (IO[bytes] | bytes): the stream, delimited or not. It must have one
            result set (the FLAT stream type, the default).
        validate_iris (bool): whether rdflib checks the IRIs. An invalid IRI is
            still read, rdflib only logs a warning. Checking slows down parsing.
        lazy (bool): read the rows during iteration instead of all at once. The
            stream must stay open until the result has been iterated, and the
            error of incomplete results is raised at the end of the iteration.

    Returns:
        JellySparqlResult: the results, an rdflib Result.

    Raises:
        JellyIncompleteResultsError: if the writer said that the results are
            incomplete, e.g., because the query failed midway. Its `result` holds
            the results read before the error.

    """
    adapter_factory = _adapter_factory(validate_iris=validate_iris)
    binding_rows = BindingRows()
    try:
        result_set = read_result_set(inp, adapter_factory, row_factory=binding_rows)
    except JellyIncompleteResultsError as error:
        # An incomplete boolean result
        result_set = cast("SparqlResultSet", error.result)
        error.result = _to_result(
            result_set, binding_rows, lazy=False, raise_error=False
        )
        raise
    return _to_result(result_set, binding_rows, lazy=lazy, raise_error=True)

An incomplete result does not stop the sequence. Instead, its error attribute is set, so check it. The results after it are still read.

def parse_jelly_sparql_sequence(
    inp: IO[bytes] | bytes, *, validate_iris: bool = False
) -> Iterator[JellySparqlResult]:
    """
    Read a sequence of SPARQL query results from one Jelly-SPARQL stream.

    This reads PUNCTUATED streams, which hold any number of results. A FLAT
    stream (the default) holds one.

    An incomplete result does not stop the sequence. Instead, its `error`
    attribute is set, so check it. The results after it are still read.

    Args:
        inp (IO[bytes] | bytes): the stream, delimited.
        validate_iris (bool): whether rdflib checks the IRIs, see
            parse_jelly_sparql().

    Yields:
        JellySparqlResult: the results, an rdflib Result for each result set.

    """
    adapter_factory = _adapter_factory(validate_iris=validate_iris)
    binding_rows = BindingRows()
    for result_set in read_result_sets(inp, adapter_factory, row_factory=binding_rows):
        yield _to_result(result_set, binding_rows, lazy=False, raise_error=False)

def serialize_jelly_sparql_sequence(
    results: Iterable[Result], out: IO[bytes], options: SparqlOptions | None = None
) -> None:
    """
    Write a sequence of SPARQL query results in one Jelly-SPARQL stream.

    The stream is PUNCTUATED, with one result set per result.

    Args:
        results (Iterable[Result]): the results.
        out (IO[bytes]): output stream.
        options (SparqlOptions | None): options of the stream, which must be
            punctuated. Defaults to SparqlOptions(punctuated=True).

    """
    if options is None:
        options = SparqlOptions(punctuated=True)
    if not options.punctuated:
        msg = "a sequence of results needs SparqlOptions(punctuated=True)"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    stream = sparql_stream(options)
    writer = FrameWriter(out, delimited=True)
    for result in results:
        _write_result(stream, result, writer)

def spo_tree(graph: Graph) -> Tree | None:
    """
    Return the graph's triples as a subject -> predicate -> objects tree.

    Only for rdflib's in-memory store, whose triples are in memory anyway. For any
    other store, return None: such a store can be far too big to group in memory.
    Its triples are then written in the store's own order, which for stores with
    indexes (e.g., Oxigraph, BerkeleyDB) is usually already grouped by subject.
    """
    store = graph.store
    if type(store) is not Memory:
        return None
    indexes = _memory_indexes(store)
    if indexes is None:
        # The private fields are not there: group with the public API
        return _group(graph.triples((None, None, None)))
    contexts = indexes.context_triples
    context = indexes.context_key(graph)
    triples = contexts.get(context)
    if not triples:
        return {}
    if not any(key not in (None, context) and value for key, value in contexts.items()):
        # The graph is alone in its store, so the store's subject-predicate-object
        # index contains its triples, already grouped and in the order they
        # were added
        return indexes.spo
    return _group(triples)

def gspo_trees(dataset: ConjunctiveGraph) -> Iterator[tuple[Any, Tree]] | None:
    """
    Return the dataset's graphs, each as its name and its triples as a tree.

    Only for rdflib's in-memory store, see spo_tree(). Each graph is grouped only
    when it's its turn, so at most one graph's tree is in memory at a time. The
    default graph is named DATASET_DEFAULT_GRAPH_ID, see dataset_quads().
    """
    store = dataset.store
    if type(store) is not Memory:
        return None
    indexes = _memory_indexes(store)
    if indexes is None:
        # The private fields are not there: group with the public API
        return _group_quads(dataset_quads(dataset))
    return _memory_gspo_trees(indexes, _default_graph_name(dataset))

def dataset_quads(dataset: ConjunctiveGraph) -> Iterator[tuple[Any, Any, Any, Any]]:
    """
    Return the dataset's quads, with graph names rather than Graph objects.

    The default graph is named DATASET_DEFAULT_GRAPH_ID. A Dataset already names
    it so, but a ConjunctiveGraph (e.g., the one rdfpipe reads into) names it
    with a random blank node. The quads of that graph go into the default graph,
    as with rdflib's TriG serializer.
    """
    default = _default_graph_name(dataset)
    for s, p, o, g in dataset.quads((None, None, None, None)):
        name = getattr(g, "identifier", g)
        if name is None or name == default:
            name = DATASET_DEFAULT_GRAPH_ID
        yield s, p, o, name
write_tree(stream, tree)

Write the statements of a subject -> predicate -> objects tree.

Uses the stream's cursor API, so the stream doesn't compare terms. In a tree, each subject differs from the one before it, and so do the predicates of one subject and the objects of one predicate. Only the first subject of the tree and the first predicate of a subject can be equal to the one before it (e.g., rdf:type as the first predicate of every subject), so only those are compared. The first object of a predicate is rarely equal to the object before it, and most predicates have only one object, so objects are not compared: an equal one is just written again.

Yields: jelly.RdfStreamFrame: full frames.

def write_tree(stream: Stream, tree: Tree) -> Iterator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]:
    """
    Write the statements of a subject -> predicate -> objects tree.

    Uses the stream's cursor API, so the stream doesn't compare terms. In a tree,
    each subject differs from the one before it, and so do the predicates of one
    subject and the objects of one predicate. Only the first subject of the tree
    and the first predicate of a subject can be equal to the one before it (e.g.,
    rdf:type as the first predicate of every subject), so only those are
    compared. The first object of a predicate is rarely equal to the object
    before it, and most predicates have only one object, so objects are not
    compared: an equal one is just written again.

    Yields:
        jelly.RdfStreamFrame: full frames.

    """
    encoder = stream.encoder
    terms = stream.repeated_terms
    first_subject = True
    for s, predicates in tree.items():
        if not first_subject or not encoder.same_term(terms[0], s):
            stream.set_subject(s)
        first_subject = False
        first_predicate = True
        for p, objects in predicates.items():
            if not first_predicate or not encoder.same_term(terms[1], p):
                stream.set_predicate(p)
            first_predicate = False
            for o in objects:
                stream.set_object(o)
                frame = stream.emit()
                if frame is not None:
                    yield frame

def write_trees(
    stream: QuadStream, trees: Iterable[tuple[Any, Tree]]
) -> Iterator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]:
    """Write the statements of graphs, see gspo_trees() and write_tree()."""
    for g, tree in trees:
        if not stream.encoder.same_term(stream.repeated_terms[3], g):
            stream.set_graph(g)
        yield from write_tree(stream, tree)

def __repr__(self) -> str:
    """
    Return the representation of StreamTypes.

    >>> repr(StreamTypes(9999, 8888))
    'StreamTypes(9999, 8888)'
    """
    with suppress(ValueError):
        physical_type_name = jelly.PhysicalStreamType.Name(self.physical_type)
        logical_type_name = jelly.LogicalStreamType.Name(self.logical_type)
        return f"StreamTypes({physical_type_name}, {logical_type_name})"
    return f"StreamTypes({self.physical_type}, {self.logical_type})"

Options for writing a Jelly-SPARQL stream.

Attributes: lookup_preset: lookup sizes. The name lookup needs at least 128 entries. rdf_version: RDF version of the terms in the stream. RDF 1.1 allows no base directions or triple terms, RDF 1.2 Basic no triple terms. punctuated: write a sequence of result sets (the PUNCTUATED stream type) instead of one result set. frame_values: maximum values (rows times variables) per frame. A frame can end earlier if the lookups fill up. delimited: write delimited frames, which files and HTTP need. A non-delimited stream is a single frame, e.g. one message for a message broker. All terms of the results must then fit in the lookups. stream_name: name of the stream.

def rows_per_frame(self, variables: int) -> int:
    """
    Compute the maximum rows per frame for this number of variables.

    >>> SparqlOptions().rows_per_frame(4)
    1024
    >>> SparqlOptions(frame_values=10).rows_per_frame(0)
    10
    """
    return max(1, self.frame_values // max(1, variables))

def stream_type_for(
    params: StreamParameters, logical_type: jelly.LogicalStreamType
) -> jelly.RdfStreamType:
    """
    Return the Jelly-RDF 1.2 stream type of a stream that is written.

    As in Jelly-JVM, a stream of graphs or datasets (the logical types GRAPHS and
    DATASETS, and their subtypes) is a stream of RDF Messages, one per graph or
    dataset.

    >>> stream_type_for(StreamParameters(), jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_FLAT_TRIPLES)
    0
    >>> stream_type_for(StreamParameters(), jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_NAMED_GRAPHS)
    1
    """
    if params.stream_type == jelly.RDF_STREAM_TYPE_MESSAGES or logical_type % 10 in (
        jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_GRAPHS,
        jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_DATASETS,
    ):
        return jelly.RDF_STREAM_TYPE_MESSAGES
    return jelly.RDF_STREAM_TYPE_FLAT

def __init__(self, decoder: Decoder) -> None:
    self.decoder = decoder
    options = decoder.options

def iter_frame(self, frame: jelly.RdfStreamFrame) -> Iterator[Any]:
    """
    Return the namespace declarations and statements of a frame.

    The stream options and the lookup entries of the frame are read right away,
    the statements as they are iterated.
    """
    message_ended = False
    rows = frame.rows
    if rows:
        if len(rows) > 1 or _ROW_WHICH_ONEOF(rows[0], "row") != "options":
            msg = (
                "a frame of a Jelly-RDF 1.2 stream can only have the stream "
                "options in its rows, in one row"
            )
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        if self.options_read:
            message_ended = self.restate_options(rows[0].options)
        else:
            self.options_read = True
    if not _FRAME_HAS_FIELD(frame, "columns"):
        return iter((MESSAGE_END,) if message_ended else ())
    if not self.options_read:
        msg = "the stream has statements before the stream options"
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    batch_rows = self.iter_batch(frame.columns)
    if message_ended:
        return chain((MESSAGE_END,), batch_rows)
    return batch_rows

def restate_options(self, options: jelly.RdfStreamOptions) -> bool:
    """
    Read restated stream options, which empty the lookups.

    Returns:
        bool: whether an RDF Message ended, because it had statements.

    """
    current = self.decoder.options
    if (
        options.version != current.params.version
        or options.physical_type != current.stream_types.physical_type
        or options.stream_type != current.params.stream_type
    ):
        msg = (
            "the protocol version, physical type and stream type must be the same "
            "in all stream options of a stream"
        )
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    self.decoder.restate_options(options)
    if self.messages and self.rows_in_message:
        self.rows_in_message = 0
        return True
    return False

def iter_batch(self, batch: jelly.RdfColumnBatch) -> Iterator[Any]:
    """Return the namespace declarations and statements of a batch."""
    rows = batch.row_count
    if rows > MAX_ROWS:
        msg = f"a frame can have at most {MAX_ROWS} statements, not {rows}"
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    lengths = self.message_lengths(batch, rows)
    # All lookup entries come first, so that the columns can refer to them
    self.ingest_entries(batch)
    namespaces = self.namespaces(batch) if batch.namespaces else []
    has_graphs = _BATCH_HAS_FIELD(batch, "graphs")
    if has_graphs and not self.quads:
        msg = "a stream of triples cannot have a graphs column"
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    subjects = self.runs(batch.subjects, rows, _RESOURCES, "subject")
    predicates = self.runs(batch.predicates, rows, _IRIS, "predicate")
    objects = self.runs(batch.objects, rows, _ANY, "object")
    graphs = None
    if self.quads:
        if has_graphs:
            graphs = self.runs(batch.graphs, rows, _RESOURCES, "graph")
        else:
            graphs = _Runs([], rows, "graph")
            graphs.add(None, rows)
        graphs.set_unbound(self.decoder.adapter.default_graph())

    # The statements of each RDF Message that ends in the batch, and the rest
    counts = [*lengths, rows - sum(lengths)]
    if lengths:
        self.rows_in_message = counts[-1]
    else:
        self.rows_in_message += rows
    statements = self.statements(counts, subjects, predicates, objects, graphs)
    if namespaces:
        return chain(namespaces, statements)
    return statements

def message_lengths(self, batch: jelly.RdfColumnBatch, rows: int) -> list[int]:
    """Return the lengths of the RDF Messages that end in a batch."""
    lengths = batch.message_lengths[:]
    if lengths:
        if not self.messages:
            msg = "message boundaries are only valid in streams of RDF Messages"
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        if sum(lengths) > rows:
            msg = (
                f"the message lengths add up to {sum(lengths)}, more than the "
                f"{rows} statements of the frame"
            )
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    return lengths

def apply_entries(self, names: Any, prefixes: Any, datatypes: Any) -> None:
    """Apply a frame's packed lookup entries."""
    decoder = self.decoder
    _apply_entries(names, decoder.names)
    _apply_entries(prefixes, decoder.prefixes)
    for entry in datatypes:
        for value in entry.values:
            if value in (LANG_STRING_DATATYPE_IRI, DIR_LANG_STRING_DATATYPE_IRI):
                msg = f"the datatype lookup cannot have {value}"
                raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    _apply_entries(datatypes, decoder.datatypes)

def statements(
    self,
    counts: list[int],
    subjects: _Runs,
    predicates: _Runs,
    objects: _Runs,
    graphs: _Runs | None,
) -> Iterator[Any]:
    """Yield the statements, `counts` at a time, with MESSAGE_END in between."""
    adapter = self.decoder.adapter
    last = len(counts) - 1
    for i, count in enumerate(counts):
        if graphs is None:
            for _ in range(count):
                yield adapter.triple(
                    (subjects.next(), predicates.next(), objects.next())
                )
        else:
            for _ in range(count):
                yield adapter.quad(
                    (
                        subjects.next(),
                        predicates.next(),
                        objects.next(),
                        graphs.next(),
                    )
                )
        if i < last:
            yield MESSAGE_END

def runs(
    self, column: jelly.RdfColumn, rows: int, allowed: int, position: str
) -> _Runs:
    """Decode a column into its runs, whose cells add up to the row count."""
    values = self.run_values(column, allowed, position)
    unbound_allowed = position == "graph"
    layouts: list[int] = column.layouts[:]
    runs = _Runs(values, rows, position)
    index = 0
    k = 0
    while k < len(layouts):
        token = layouts[k]
        k += 1
        length = token & _LENGTH_MASK
        if length == _LENGTH_MASK:
            if k == len(layouts):
                msg = (
                    f"corrupt layout of the {position} column: a length is cut off"
                )
                raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
            length += layouts[k]
            k += 1
        skip = token >> _SKIP_SHIFT
        if index + skip > len(values):
            msg = (
                f"corrupt layout of the {position} column: it skips past its values"
            )
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        runs.add_values(index, skip)
        index += skip
        if token & _UNBOUND:
            if not unbound_allowed:
                raise _unbound(position)
            runs.add(None, length + 1)
        elif index < len(values):
            runs.add(values[index], length + 2)
            index += 1
        else:
            msg = (
                f"corrupt layout of the {position} column: a repeated value is "
                "past its values"
            )
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    runs.add_values(index, len(values) - index)
    if runs.cells < rows:
        if not unbound_allowed:
            raise _unbound(position)
        runs.add(None, rows - runs.cells)
    return runs

def cells(self, column: jelly.RdfColumn, rows: int, position: str) -> list[Any]:
    """
    Decode a Jelly-SPARQL column into its cells, in order.

    The column may hold terms of any type. Unbound cells are None.
    """
    values = self.run_values(column, _ANY, position)
    layouts: list[int] = column.layouts[:]
    # Without layout tokens, each value fills one cell
    cells = _layout_cells(values, layouts, rows, position) if layouts else values
    if len(cells) > rows:
        raise _too_many_cells(position)
    if len(cells) < rows:
        # Pad with unbound cells
        cells += [None] * (rows - len(cells))
    return cells

def run_values(
    self, column: jelly.RdfColumn, allowed: int, position: str
) -> list[Any]:
    """Decode the run values of a column, in order."""
    counts = (
        len(column.name_ids),
        len(column.lex_values),
        len(column.bnodes),
        len(column.triple_terms),
    )
    for kind in range(4):
        if counts[kind] and not allowed & (1 << kind):
            msg = f"the {position} column cannot have {_KIND_NAMES[kind]}"
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    if column.kinds:
        return self.mixed_values(column, counts, position)
    if sum(1 for count in counts if count) > 1:
        msg = f"the {position} column has terms of more than one type, but no kinds"
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    if counts[_KIND_LITERAL]:
        return self.literals(column)
    if counts[_KIND_BNODE]:
        return self.bnodes(column)
    if counts[_KIND_TRIPLE]:
        return self.triple_terms(column)
    return self.iris(column)

def mixed_values(
    self, column: jelly.RdfColumn, counts: tuple[int, ...], position: str
) -> list[Any]:
    """Decode the run values of a column whose kinds say which type each is."""
    kinds: bytes = column.kinds
    value_count = sum(counts)
    _check_kinds(kinds, value_count, position)
    iris = self.iris(column)
    literals = self.literals(column)
    bnodes = self.bnodes(column)
    triple_terms = self.triple_terms(column)
    # How many values of each type were taken. If no type runs out of values,
    # all are used up at the end, as there are value_count of them
    iri = literal = bnode = triple = 0
    values: list[Any] = []
    for i in range(value_count):
        kind = (kinds[i >> 2] >> ((i & 3) << 1)) & 3
        if kind == _KIND_IRI:
            if iri == len(iris):
                raise _kinds_mismatch(position, kind)
            values.append(iris[iri])
            iri += 1
        elif kind == _KIND_LITERAL:
            if literal == len(literals):
                raise _kinds_mismatch(position, kind)
            values.append(literals[literal])
            literal += 1
        elif kind == _KIND_BNODE:
            if bnode == len(bnodes):
                raise _kinds_mismatch(position, kind)
            values.append(bnodes[bnode])
            bnode += 1
        else:
            if triple == len(triple_terms):
                raise _kinds_mismatch(position, kind)
            values.append(triple_terms[triple])
            triple += 1
    return values

def literal_kind(self, kind: int, langtags: Any, directions: Any) -> _LiteralKind:
    """Resolve a literal kind: its language tag, datatype and base direction."""
    decoder = self.decoder
    if not kind:
        return _LiteralKind(decoder, None, None, None)
    if kind & 1:
        index = (kind + 1) >> 1
        if index > decoder.datatypes.lookup_size:
            msg = (
                f"a literal kind refers to datatype {index}, which is outside the "
                "datatype lookup"
            )
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        datatype = decoder.datatypes.at(index)
        return _LiteralKind(decoder, None, datatype, None)
    index = (kind >> 1) - 1
    if index >= len(langtags):
        msg = f"a literal kind refers to language tag {index}, which is not there"
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    direction = None
    if directions and directions[index]:
        direction = self.direction(directions[index])
    return _LiteralKind(decoder, langtags[index] or None, None, direction)

def __init__(self, adapter: Adapter) -> None:
    """
    Initialize decoder.

    Initializes decoder with lookup tables of preset sizes and an
    integration-dependent adapter.

    Args:
        adapter (Adapter): integration-dependent adapter that specifies terms
        conversion to specific objects, framing,
        namespace declarations, and graphs/datasets forming.

    """
    self.adapter = adapter
    self.new_lookups()
    # The last s, p, o and g terms, for repeated terms
    self.repeated_terms: list[object] = [_MISSING] * 4
    # Literals often repeat (e.g., the same values in many entities), and
    # making one is often slow (rdflib parses the value). By language tag and
    # datatype, then by lexical form, see literal_cache()
    self.literal_caches: dict[tuple[str | None, str | None], dict[str, Any]] = {}
    self.literal_cache_size = 0

    self.term_handlers: dict[type[Any], TermHandler] = {
        t: getattr(self, name) for t, name in self._TERM_HANDLER_NAMES.items()
    }
    #: Decodes the frames of Jelly-RDF 1.2 streams, None for older ones
    self.column_decoder: ColumnDecoder | None = None
    if not is_row_layout(self.options.params.version):
        self.column_decoder = ColumnDecoder(self)

def new_lookups(self) -> None:
    """Make empty lookups, of the sizes in the options."""
    lookup_preset = self.options.lookup_preset
    self.names = LookupDecoder(lookup_size=lookup_preset.max_names)
    self.prefixes = LookupDecoder(lookup_size=lookup_preset.max_prefixes)
    self.datatypes = LookupDecoder(lookup_size=lookup_preset.max_datatypes)
    # One IRI term per name table entry: an IRI is often
    # used with the same prefix again, so its term can be reused. Index 0 is
    # unused, as table indices start from 1
    self.iri_cache: list[_CachedIri | None] = [None] * (lookup_preset.max_names + 1)

def iter_row_layout(self, frame: jelly.RdfStreamFrame) -> Iterator[Any]:
    """Yield the decoded rows of a frame of a Jelly-RDF 1.0 or 1.1 stream."""
    # Rows are told apart by the name of their field, most common ones first
    for row_owner in frame.rows:
        kind: str | None = _ROW_WHICH_ONEOF(row_owner, "row")
        if kind == "triple":
            yield self.decode_triple(row_owner.triple)
        elif kind == "quad":
            yield self.decode_quad(row_owner.quad)
        elif kind == "name":
            self.ingest_name_entry(row_owner.name)
        elif kind == "prefix":
            self.ingest_prefix_entry(row_owner.prefix)
        elif kind == "datatype":
            self.ingest_datatype_entry(row_owner.datatype)
        elif kind == "namespace":
            yield self.decode_namespace_declaration(row_owner.namespace)
        else:
            self.decode_other_row(row_owner, kind)

def validate_stream_options(self, options: jelly.RdfStreamOptions) -> None:
    """Check that repeated stream options are the same as the first ones."""
    stream_types, lookup_preset, params = self.options
    if (
        stream_types.physical_type != options.physical_type
        or stream_types.logical_type != options.logical_type
        or params.stream_name != options.stream_name
        or params.version < options.version
        or lookup_preset.max_prefixes != options.max_prefix_table_size
        or lookup_preset.max_datatypes != options.max_datatype_table_size
        or lookup_preset.max_names != options.max_name_table_size
    ):

        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)

def decode_iri(self, iri: jelly.RdfIri) -> Any:
    """
    Decode RdfIri message to IRI using a custom adapter.

    The term is reused if the same name and prefix entries were decoded
    before, so the adapter's IRI terms must be immutable.

    Args:
        iri (jelly.RdfIri): RdfIri message

    Returns:
        Any: IRI, based on adapter implementation, e.g., rdflib.term.URIRef

    """
    names = self.names
    name_index = iri.name_id or names.last_reused_index + 1
    name = names.decode_name_term_index(name_index)
    prefix = self.prefixes.decode_prefix_term_index(iri.prefix_id)
    # The lookup tables keep the strings they were given, so the same objects
    # mean the same entries (or at least equal strings, which is just as good)
    cached = self.iri_cache[name_index]
    if cached is not None and cached.name is name and cached.prefix is prefix:
        return cached.term
    return self.new_iri(name_index, name, prefix)

def decode_literal(self, literal: jelly.RdfLiteral) -> Any:
    """
    Decode RdfLiteral to literal based on custom adapter implementation.

    Recently decoded literals are reused, so the adapter's literal terms must
    be immutable.

    Args:

    language = datatype = None

    elif kind == "datatype":
        datatype = self.datatypes.decode_datatype_term_index(literal.datatype)
    lex = literal.lex

    term = cache.get(lex)
    if term is None:

    return term

def new_literal(
    self,
    lex: str,
    language: str | None,
    datatype: str | None,
    cache: dict[str, Any],
) -> Any:
    """Make a literal term, and keep it in its literal_cache()."""
    term = self.adapter.literal(lex=lex, language=language, datatype=datatype)
    if self.literal_cache_size >= LITERAL_CACHE_SIZE:
        for full in self.literal_caches.values():
            full.clear()
        self.literal_cache_size = 0
    cache[lex] = term
    self.literal_cache_size += 1
    return term

    Decode the terms of a triple or quad message.

    Notes: also updates the repeated terms

    Args:
        fields (list[Any]): the message's fields, from ListFields()
        size (int): 3 for a triple, 4 for a quad

    Raises:
        JellyConformanceError: if a missing repeated term is encountered

    Returns:
        Any: a list of decoded terms

    """
    repeated = self.repeated_terms
    terms = repeated[:size]
    # The fields come in the order of their numbers, so the terms are decoded
    # in s, p, o, g order. Each term has four fields, numbered from 1:
    # IRI, blank node, literal and quoted triple (s_iri = 1, ..., o_iri = 9),
    # but the graph's are IRI, blank node, default graph and literal
    for field, value in fields:
        number: int = field.number - 1
        position = number >> 2
        kind = number & 3
        if kind == _IRI:
            term = self.decode_iri(value)
        elif kind == _BNODE:
            term = self.adapter.bnode(value)
        elif kind == _LITERAL_OR_DEFAULT_GRAPH:
            if position == _GRAPH:
                term = self.adapter.default_graph()
            else:
                term = self.decode_literal(value)
        elif position == _GRAPH:
            term = self.decode_literal(value)
        else:
            term = self.decode_quoted_triple(value)
        terms[position] = term
        repeated[position] = term
    for i in range(size):
        if terms[i] is _MISSING:
            msg = f"missing repeated term {_POSITIONS[i]}"
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    return terms

def check_stream_options(options: jelly.RdfStreamOptions) -> None:
    """
    Check that the parser can read a stream with these options.

    The fields of one layout must not be set in a stream of the
    other. The lookups must not be larger than the parser allows (see the
    MAX_*_LOOKUP_SIZE constants).

    Raises:
        JellyConformanceError: if it can't.

    """
    version = options.version
    if not MIN_VERSION <= version <= MAX_VERSION:
        msg = (
            f"unsupported protocol version {version}, "
            f"expected {MIN_VERSION} to {MAX_VERSION}"
        )
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    physical_type = options.physical_type
    if physical_type not in _PHYSICAL_TYPES:
        msg = f"unknown physical stream type: {physical_type}"
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    if is_row_layout(version):
        if options.stream_type or options.rdf_version:
            msg = (
                "the stream type and RDF version are only valid in Jelly-RDF 1.2 "
                "streams (protocol version 3)"
            )
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        if options.logical_type not in _LOGICAL_TYPES:
            msg = f"unknown logical stream type: {options.logical_type}"
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        min_names = MIN_NAME_LOOKUP_SIZE
    else:
        if options.generalized_statements or options.rdf_star or options.logical_type:
            msg = (
                "generalized statements, RDF-star and logical stream types are only "
                "valid in Jelly-RDF 1.0 and 1.1 streams (protocol versions 1 and 2)"
            )
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        if physical_type == jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_GRAPHS:
            msg = "Jelly-RDF 1.2 streams cannot be of the GRAPHS physical type"
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        if options.stream_type not in (
            jelly.RDF_STREAM_TYPE_FLAT,
            jelly.RDF_STREAM_TYPE_MESSAGES,
        ):
            msg = f"unknown stream type: {options.stream_type}"
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        if options.rdf_version not in _RDF_VERSIONS:
            msg = f"unknown RDF version: {options.rdf_version}"
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        min_names = MIN_COLUMN_NAME_LOOKUP_SIZE
    _check_size("name", options.max_name_table_size, min_names, MAX_NAME_LOOKUP_SIZE)
    _check_size("prefix", options.max_prefix_table_size, 0, MAX_PREFIX_LOOKUP_SIZE)
    _check_size(
        "datatype", options.max_datatype_table_size, 0, MAX_DATATYPE_LOOKUP_SIZE
    )

def parser_options(
    options: jelly.RdfStreamOptions, *, delimited: bool

    Return the parser options of a stream, after checking them.

            stream_type=options.stream_type,

    )

    *,

def messages(rows: Iterable[Iterable[Any]]) -> Iterator[list[Any]]:
    """
    Group the rows of a stream of RDF Messages by message.

    Args:
        rows (Iterable[Iterable[Any]]): the rows that Decoder.iter_rows() returns
            for each frame, and Decoder.end_of_stream()

    Yields:
        list[Any]: the namespace declarations and statements of each message

    """
    message: list[Any] = []
    for frame_rows in rows:
        for row in frame_rows:
            if row is MESSAGE_END:
                yield message
                message = []
            else:
                message.append(row)
