def flat_rows(rows: Iterable[Iterable[Any]], options: ParserOptions) -> Iterator[Any]:
    """
    Return the rows of all frames, without the ends of RDF Messages.

    Args:
        rows (Iterable[Iterable[Any]]): the rows that Decoder.iter_rows() returns
            for each frame, and Decoder.end_of_stream()
        options (ParserOptions): the stream's options

    """
    # Not a generator: the rows of the frames reach the caller without passing
    # through one more Python frame
    all_rows = chain.from_iterable(rows)
    if options.params.stream_type == jelly.RDF_STREAM_TYPE_MESSAGES:
        return filter(partial(is_not, MESSAGE_END), all_rows)
    return all_rows

def single_byte_tags(descriptor: Descriptor) -> frozenset[int]:
    """
    Return the single-byte tags that a message's fields can have.

    Only fields numbered 1 to 15 have a one-byte tag. A repeated scalar field
    may be written packed or not, so both of its tags are returned.

    Args:
        descriptor (Descriptor): descriptor of the message

    Returns:
        frozenset[int]: tag bytes of the message's fields

    """
    tags = set()
    for field in descriptor.fields:
        if field.number > _MAX_SINGLE_BYTE_FIELD:
            continue
        tags.add((field.number << 3) | _WIRE_TYPES.get(field.type, _WIRE_VARINT))
        if field.is_repeated:
            tags.add((field.number << 3) | _WIRE_LENGTH_DELIMITED)
    return frozenset(tags)

def hint_bytes_needed(first_byte: int, tags: frozenset[int] = FRAME_TAGS) -> int:
    """
    Return how many bytes `delimited_jelly_hint` needs to decide.

    Args:
        first_byte (int): first byte of the stream
        tags (frozenset[int]): tag bytes a frame can start with

    Returns:
        int: number of bytes to read from the start of the stream, at most 128

    >>> hint_bytes_needed(0x11)
    1

    >>> hint_bytes_needed(0x0A)
    11

    """
    if first_byte in tags:
        return first_byte + 1
    return 1

docs.title: delimited_jelly_hint(header, tags=FRAME_TAGS)
docs.text:
Detect whether a Jelly stream is delimited, from its first bytes.

A non-delimited stream is a single frame, so it starts with the tag of one of the frame's fields -- any of them, because a writer may put the fields in any order. A delimited stream starts with the size of its first frame. So, if the first byte is not a frame tag, the stream is delimited. Otherwise it may still be the size of a small first frame, of at most 127 bytes: the stream is then delimited if the bytes after it are exactly that many bytes of frame fields.

Pass as much of the start of the stream as you have, up to 128 bytes -- hint_bytes_needed tells you how much is actually needed once you have the first byte. Given fewer bytes than the check needs, the stream is reported as non-delimited.

Args: header (bytes): first bytes of the stream tags (frozenset[int]): tag bytes a frame can start with, FRAME_TAGS for Jelly-RDF and SPARQL_FRAME_TAGS for Jelly-SPARQL

Returns: bool: True if the stream is delimited

An empty stream is an empty non-delimited frame:

delimited_jelly_hint(b"") False

0x11 is not a frame tag, so it is the size of the first frame:

delimited_jelly_hint(bytes([0x11, 0x0A, 0x0F, 0x0A, 0x0D])) True

A 10-byte frame holding one name entry, written non-delimited. It starts with the tag of the rows field, and the 9 bytes after it are not a whole frame of 10 bytes:

frame = bytes([0x0A, 0x08, 0x4A, 0x06, 0x12, 0x04, 0x6E, 0x61, 0x6D, 0x65]) delimited_jelly_hint(frame) False

The same frame written delimited. Its size, 10, is also the tag of the rows field, but the 10 bytes after it are exactly one frame's worth of fields:

delimited_jelly_hint(bytes([0x0A]) + frame) True

A stream of empty delimited frames is delimited too -- 0 is never a tag:

delimited_jelly_hint(bytes([0x00, 0x00, 0x00])) True

Two bytes of garbage are not enough to tell, so they count as a frame:

delimited_jelly_hint(bytes([0x12, 0x34])) False

def delimited_jelly_hint(header: bytes, tags: frozenset[int] = FRAME_TAGS) -> bool:
    """
    Detect whether a Jelly stream is delimited, from its first bytes.

    A non-delimited stream is a single frame, so it starts with the tag of one
    of the frame's fields -- any of them, because a writer may put the fields
    in any order. A delimited stream starts with the size of its first frame.
    So, if the first byte is not a frame tag, the stream is delimited.
    Otherwise it may still be the size of a small first frame, of at most 127
    bytes: the stream is then delimited if the bytes after it are exactly that
    many bytes of frame fields.

    Pass as much of the start of the stream as you have, up to 128 bytes --
    `hint_bytes_needed` tells you how much is actually needed once you have the
    first byte. Given fewer bytes than the check needs, the stream is reported
    as non-delimited.

    Args:
        header (bytes): first bytes of the stream
        tags (frozenset[int]): tag bytes a frame can start with, FRAME_TAGS for
            Jelly-RDF and SPARQL_FRAME_TAGS for Jelly-SPARQL

    Returns:
        bool: True if the stream is delimited

    An empty stream is an empty non-delimited frame:

    >>> delimited_jelly_hint(b"")
    False

    0x11 is not a frame tag, so it is the size of the first frame:

    >>> delimited_jelly_hint(bytes([0x11, 0x0A, 0x0F, 0x0A, 0x0D]))
    True

    A 10-byte frame holding one name entry, written non-delimited. It starts
    with the tag of the rows field, and the 9 bytes after it are not a whole
    frame of 10 bytes:

    >>> frame = bytes([0x0A, 0x08, 0x4A, 0x06, 0x12, 0x04, 0x6E, 0x61, 0x6D, 0x65])
    >>> delimited_jelly_hint(frame)
    False

    The same frame written delimited. Its size, 10, is also the tag of the rows
    field, but the 10 bytes after it are exactly one frame's worth of fields:

    >>> delimited_jelly_hint(bytes([0x0A]) + frame)
    True

    A stream of empty delimited frames is delimited too -- 0 is never a tag:

    >>> delimited_jelly_hint(bytes([0x00, 0x00, 0x00]))
    True

    Two bytes of garbage are not enough to tell, so they count as a frame:

    >>> delimited_jelly_hint(bytes([0x12, 0x34]))
    False

    """
    if not header:
        return False
    first = header[0]
    if first not in tags:
        # Not a frame tag, so it is the size of the first frame. This includes
        # 0, an empty frame: a stream of only empty frames is delimited too.
        return True
    if len(header) < first + 1:
        return False
    return _is_frame_fields(header[1 : first + 1], tags)

def read_hint_header(inp: IO[bytes], tags: frozenset[int] = FRAME_TAGS) -> bytes:
    """
    Read just enough of the start of the stream to detect delimiting.

    Reads one byte, and at most 128. Pass the result to `delimited_jelly_hint`.

    Args:
        inp (IO[bytes]): stream to read from
        tags (frozenset[int]): tag bytes a frame can start with

    Returns:
        bytes: bytes read from the start of the stream

    """
    header = inp.read(1)
    if not header:
        return header
    remaining = hint_bytes_needed(header[0], tags) - 1
    if remaining:
        header += _read_exactly(inp, remaining)
    return header

Detect from the first bytes whether a stream is delimited.

Args: inp (IO[bytes]): the stream tags (frozenset[int]): tag bytes a frame can start with

Returns: tuple[IO[bytes], bool]: a stream positioned at the start again, and whether it is delimited

Source code in pyjelly/parse/ioutils.py 
def detect_delimited(
    inp: IO[bytes], tags: frozenset[int] = FRAME_TAGS
) -> tuple[IO[bytes], bool]:
    """
    Detect from the first bytes whether a stream is delimited.

    Args:
        inp (IO[bytes]): the stream
        tags (frozenset[int]): tag bytes a frame can start with

    Returns:
        tuple[IO[bytes], bool]: a stream positioned at the start again, and
            whether it is delimited

    """
    if inp.seekable():
        header = read_hint_header(inp, tags)
        inp.seek(-len(header), os.SEEK_CUR)
    else:
        # Input may not be seekable (e.g. a network stream). Then the bytes we read
        # are put back in front of it. Only an unbuffered stream gets a buffer: a
        # second buffer around a buffered stream (e.g. from socket.makefile())
        # waits for the inner one to fill up, which blocks streaming.
        # See also: https://github.com/Jelly-RDF/pyjelly/issues/298
        buffered = inp
        if not isinstance(inp, io.BufferedIOBase):
            buffered = io.BufferedReader(inp)  # type: ignore[arg-type, type-var, unused-ignore]
        header = read_hint_header(buffered, tags)
        inp = _StreamWithHeader(header, buffered)  # type: ignore[assignment]
    return inp, delimited_jelly_hint(header, tags)

def parse_delimited(message_class: type[MessageT], inp: IO[bytes]) -> MessageT | None:
    """
    Read the next length-prefixed message, or None at the end of the input.

    Raises:
        DecodeError: if the bytes are not a message of the class, or the input
            ends in the middle of one. Or UnicodeDecodeError, see DECODE_ERRORS.
        ValueError: if the input is closed.

    """
    try:
        # protobuf annotates `input_bytes` as io.BytesIO, but any IO[bytes] works.
        return parse_length_prefixed(message_class, inp)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    except DECODE_ERRORS:
        raise
    except (ValueError, OverflowError) as error:
        if getattr(inp, "closed", False):
            raise
        # The length prefix is cut short, or too large to read
        msg = f"invalid length prefix ({error})"
        raise DecodeError(msg) from None

The options are in the first frame that has rows. A stream with no such frame (e.g., an empty file) is an empty graph, with the options of an empty Jelly-RDF 1.2 stream of triples.

Args: inp (IO[bytes]): jelly buffered binary stream

Raises: JellyConformanceError: if the parser can't read the stream

Returns: tuple[ParserOptions, Iterator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]]: ParserOptions holds: stream types, lookup presets and other stream options

Source code in pyjelly/parse/ioutils.py 
def get_options_and_frames(
    inp: IO[bytes],
) -> tuple[ParserOptions, Iterator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]]:
    """
    Return stream options and frames from the buffered binary stream.

    The options are in the first frame that has rows. A stream with no such frame
    (e.g., an empty file) is an empty graph, with the options of an empty
    Jelly-RDF 1.2 stream of triples.

    Args:
        inp (IO[bytes]): jelly buffered binary stream

    Raises:
        JellyConformanceError: if the parser can't read the stream

    Returns:
        tuple[ParserOptions, Iterator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]]: ParserOptions holds:
            stream types, lookup presets and other stream options

    """
    inp, is_delimited = detect_delimited(inp)

    if is_delimited:
        first_frame = None
        skipped_frames = []
        frames = frame_iterator(inp)
        for frame in frames:
            if not frame.rows:
                skipped_frames.append(frame)
            else:
                first_frame = frame
                break
        if first_frame is None:
            return _empty_stream_options(delimited=True), iter(skipped_frames)

        options = options_from_frame(first_frame, delimited=True)
        return options, chain(skipped_frames, (first_frame,), frames)

    try:
        frame = parse(jelly.RdfStreamFrame, inp.read())
    except DECODE_ERRORS as error:
        raise _not_jelly(error) from None

    if not frame.rows:
        return _empty_stream_options(delimited=False), iter((frame,))

    options = options_from_frame(frame, delimited=False)
    return options, iter((frame,))

def __init__(
    self,
    adapter_factory: AdapterFactory,
    *,
    row_factory: RowFactory = tuple_rows,
    max_rows: int = MAX_SPARQL_FRAME_ROWS,
    max_values: int = MAX_SPARQL_FRAME_VALUES,
) -> None:
    self.adapter_factory = adapter_factory
    self.row_factory = row_factory
    self.max_rows = min(max_rows, MAX_ROWS)
    self.max_values = max_values
    #: Stream options, once read
    self.options: jelly.SparqlResultsOptions | None = None
    self.decoder: Decoder | None = None
    self.columns: ColumnDecoder | None = None
    #: Whether the stream is a sequence of result sets

    # Variables declared by the first header of the result set, and whether a
    # header is in effect. Repeated stream options cancel the header.
    self.variables: list[str] | None = None
    self.header_in_effect = False
    # Whether the next frame starts a result set, whether the current result
    # set is a boolean result, and whether a trailer came after the options
    self.result_set_start = True
    self.boolean_read = False

def decode(self, frame: jelly.SparqlResultsFrame) -> DecodedFrame:
    """Decode a frame."""
    out = DecodedFrame()
    has_options = _FRAME_HAS_FIELD(frame, "options")
    if has_options:
        self.read_options(frame.options)
    elif self.options is None:
        msg = "the stream does not start with the stream options"
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    elif self.trailer_read and not self.punctuated:
        msg = (
            "a frame after the trailer must have the stream options: the trailer "
            "ends the result set"
        )
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    if self.result_set_start:
        self.start_result_set()
        out.starts = True
    if self.boolean_read:
        msg = "no frame of the result set can follow its boolean result"
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    if _FRAME_HAS_FIELD(frame, "ask_result"):
        self.read_boolean(frame, out)
    else:
        self.read_solutions(frame, has_options=has_options, out=out)
    links = frame.metadata.get(LINK_KEY)
    if links is not None:
        out.links = decode_links(links)
    if _FRAME_HAS_FIELD(frame, "trailer"):
        out.trailer = frame.trailer.error
        self.trailer_read = True
        self.result_set_start = self.punctuated
    else:
        self.result_set_start = False
    return out

def read_options(self, options: jelly.SparqlResultsOptions) -> None:
    """Read the stream options. Repeated options also empty the lookups."""
    check_sparql_options(options)
    punctuated = options.stream_type == jelly.SPARQL_STREAM_TYPE_PUNCTUATED
    parser_options = sparql_parser_options(options)
    current = self.options
    if current is None:
        decoder = Decoder(self.adapter_factory(parser_options))
        self.decoder = decoder
        self.columns = decoder.column_decoder
    else:
        if options.stream_type != current.stream_type:
            msg = "the stream type must be the same in all stream options"
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        if punctuated and not self.result_set_start:
            msg = (
                "in a PUNCTUATED stream, the stream options can only be repeated "
                "in the first frame of a result set"
            )
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        current_decoder = self.decoder
        assert current_decoder is not None
        current_decoder.adapter.options = parser_options
        current_decoder.new_lookups()
        self.header_in_effect = False
    self.options = options
    self.punctuated = punctuated
    if not punctuated:
        self.trailer_read = False

def start_result_set(self) -> None:
    """Reset the per-result-set state, for the next result set."""
    self.variables = None
    self.header_in_effect = False
    self.boolean_read = False
    self.trailer_read = False
    if self.result_sets:
        # Each result set has its own blank node labels
        columns = self.columns
        assert columns is not None
        columns.bnode_scope = f"r{self.result_sets}-"
    self.result_sets += 1

def read_variables(
    self, frame: jelly.SparqlResultsFrame, *, has_options: bool
) -> list[str]:
    """Read the frame's header, if any, and return the current variables."""
    if frame.variables:
        if not has_options and not self.result_set_start:
            msg = (
                "the variables can only be declared in the first frame of a "
                "result set, or in a frame with the stream options"
            )
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        self.read_header(list(frame.variables))
    elif not self.header_in_effect:
        # A missing header next to the options, or at the start of a result
        # set, means zero variables
        if self.variables:
            msg = (
                "the frame repeats the stream options, so it must repeat the "
                "variables too"
            )
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        self.read_header([])
    variables = self.variables
    assert variables is not None
    return variables

def next(self) -> DecodedFrame | None:
    """Return the next frame, or None at the end of the stream."""
    frame = self.pending
    if frame is not None:
        self.pending = None
        return frame
    message = next(self.frames, None)
    if message is None:
        return None
    return self.decoder.decode(message)

docs.title: SparqlResultSet(reader, first)
docs.text:
One result set of a Jelly-SPARQL stream: a solution sequence or a boolean result.

Rows are read from the stream lazily, during iteration. Each row is a tuple with one value per variable, None if the variable is unbound. A loop that stops early can be resumed later. Once all rows have been read, iterating again raises an error. If the next result set is read first, the unread rows are kept in memory.

If the producer ended the result set with an error, iterating raises JellyIncompleteResultsError after the last row, and so does boolean. If the stream ends without a trailer, truncated is set and a JellyTruncatedResultsWarning is issued.

def __init__(self, reader: ResultSetReader, first: DecodedFrame) -> None:
    self.reader = reader
    self.first: DecodedFrame | None = first
    #: Variables in projection order. Empty for a boolean result.
    self.variables: list[str] = first.variables
    self._boolean = first.boolean
    #: Link IRIs for the result set (head.link in SPARQL JSON)
    self.links: list[str] = first.links or []
    #: Error message from the producer, if the result set is incomplete
    self.error = ""
    #: Whether the stream ended without a trailer, so rows may be missing.
    #: Only known after all rows have been read.
    self.truncated = False
    # Row lists of the coming frames, and the unread rows of the current one
    self._frames = self._read()
    self._rows: Iterator[Any] = iter(())
    # Whether an iteration has read all rows
    self._done = False
    if first.boolean is not None:
        # A boolean result is a single frame, so its trailer is already known
        if first.trailer:
            self.error = first.trailer
        elif first.trailer is None:
            self._truncated()

def collect(self, rows: list[Any]) -> None:
    """
    Append all remaining rows to a list. Faster than iterating.

    Raises:
        JellyIncompleteResultsError: if the result set is incomplete. The rows
            are appended first.

    """
    self._check_not_done()
    rows.extend(self._rows)
    for frame_rows in self._frames:
        rows.extend(frame_rows)
    self._end()

Source code in pyjelly/parse/sparql.py 
def keep(self) -> None:
    """Read the remaining rows into memory, for iteration later."""
    if not self._done:
        kept = list(self._rows)
        for rows in self._frames:
            kept += rows
        self._rows = iter(kept)

def tuple_rows(variables: list[str], cells: list[list[Any]], rows: int) -> list[Any]:

def check_sparql_options(options: jelly.SparqlResultsOptions) -> None:
    """
    Check that this parser supports a Jelly-SPARQL stream with these options.

    Raises:
        JellyConformanceError: if it can't.

    """
    version = options.version
    if not 1 <= version <= SPARQL_MAX_VERSION:
        msg = (
            f"unsupported Jelly-SPARQL version {version}, "
            f"expected 1 to {SPARQL_MAX_VERSION}"
        )
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    if options.stream_type not in _STREAM_TYPES:
        msg = f"unknown stream type: {options.stream_type}"
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    if options.rdf_version not in _RDF_VERSIONS:
        msg = f"unknown RDF version: {options.rdf_version}"
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    _check_size(
        "name",
        options.max_name_table_size,
        MIN_COLUMN_NAME_LOOKUP_SIZE,
        MAX_NAME_LOOKUP_SIZE,
    )
    _check_size("prefix", options.max_prefix_table_size, 0, MAX_PREFIX_LOOKUP_SIZE)
    _check_size(
        "datatype", options.max_datatype_table_size, 0, MAX_DATATYPE_LOOKUP_SIZE
    )

def sparql_parser_options(options: jelly.SparqlResultsOptions) -> ParserOptions:
    """
    Build the adapter options for a Jelly-SPARQL stream.

    Terms are decoded like in a Jelly-RDF 1.2 stream with the same lookup sizes and
    RDF version. The stream types are left unspecified.

    return ParserOptions(
        stream_types=StreamTypes(),
        lookup_preset=LookupPreset(
            max_names=options.max_name_table_size,
            max_prefixes=options.max_prefix_table_size,
            max_datatypes=options.max_datatype_table_size,

        params=StreamParameters(
            version=VERSION_1_2,
            stream_name=options.stream_name,
            rdf_version=options.rdf_version,

    )

def decode_links(value: bytes) -> list[str] | None:
    r"""
    Split the "link" metadata value into IRIs. Return None if it isn't UTF-8.

    >>> decode_links(b"http://example.org/a\nhttp://example.org/b")
    ['http://example.org/a', 'http://example.org/b']
    >>> decode_links(b"")
    []
    >>> decode_links(b"\xff") is None
    True
    """
    try:
        text = value.decode()
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return None
    return text.split("\n") if text else []

def sparql_frames(inp: IO[bytes] | bytes) -> Iterator[jelly.SparqlResultsFrame]:
    """
    Iterate the frames of a Jelly-SPARQL stream, delimited or not.

    Raises:
        JellyConformanceError: if the stream is empty, or isn't Jelly-SPARQL.

    """
    if isinstance(inp, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
        inp = io.BytesIO(inp)
    inp, delimited = detect_delimited(inp, SPARQL_FRAME_TAGS)
    if not delimited:
        data = inp.read()
        if not data:
            msg = "the stream is empty, but it must have at least one frame"
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        try:
            return iter((parse(jelly.SparqlResultsFrame, data),))
        except DECODE_ERRORS as error:
            raise _not_sparql(error) from None
    return _delimited_frames(inp)

A FLAT stream (the default) has one result set, a PUNCTUATED stream any number. Moving on to the next result set reads the rest of the current one and keeps its unread rows in memory.

Args: inp (IO[bytes] | bytes): the stream, delimited or not. adapter_factory (AdapterFactory): builds the term adapter from the stream options. row_factory (RowFactory): builds the rows. Tuples by default. max_rows (int): maximum rows per frame. max_values (int): maximum values (rows times variables) per frame.

Yields: SparqlResultSet: the result sets, in order.

Source code in pyjelly/parse/sparql.py 
def read_result_sets(
    inp: IO[bytes] | bytes,
    adapter_factory: AdapterFactory,
    *,
    row_factory: RowFactory = tuple_rows,
    max_rows: int = MAX_SPARQL_FRAME_ROWS,
    max_values: int = MAX_SPARQL_FRAME_VALUES,
) -> Iterator[SparqlResultSet]:
    """
    Read the result sets of a Jelly-SPARQL stream.

    A FLAT stream (the default) has one result set, a PUNCTUATED stream any
    number. Moving on to the next result set reads the rest of the current one
    and keeps its unread rows in memory.

    Args:
        inp (IO[bytes] | bytes): the stream, delimited or not.
        adapter_factory (AdapterFactory): builds the term adapter from the stream
            options.
        row_factory (RowFactory): builds the rows. Tuples by default.
        max_rows (int): maximum rows per frame.
        max_values (int): maximum values (rows times variables) per frame.

    Yields:
        SparqlResultSet: the result sets, in order.

    """
    decoder = SparqlDecoder(
        adapter_factory,
        row_factory=row_factory,
        max_rows=max_rows,
        max_values=max_values,
    )
    reader = ResultSetReader(sparql_frames(inp), decoder)
    while (first := reader.next()) is not None:
        result_set = SparqlResultSet(reader, first)
        yield result_set
        result_set.keep()

def read_result_set(
    inp: IO[bytes] | bytes,
    adapter_factory: AdapterFactory,
    *,
    row_factory: RowFactory = tuple_rows,
    max_rows: int = MAX_SPARQL_FRAME_ROWS,
    max_values: int = MAX_SPARQL_FRAME_VALUES,
) -> SparqlResultSet:
    """
    Read the single result set of a FLAT Jelly-SPARQL stream.

    The first frame is read now, the rows during iteration. For PUNCTUATED
    streams, use read_result_sets().

    Raises:
        JellyConformanceError: if the stream is PUNCTUATED.
        JellyIncompleteResultsError: for a boolean result that the producer
            could not complete.

    """
    result_sets = read_result_sets(
        inp,
        adapter_factory,
        row_factory=row_factory,
        max_rows=max_rows,
        max_values=max_values,
    )
    result_set = next(result_sets)
    if result_set.reader.decoder.punctuated:
        msg = (
            "the stream is a sequence of result sets (PUNCTUATED). Read it with "
            "parse_jelly_sparql_sequence() of pyjelly.integrations.rdflib.sparql "
            "or pyjelly.integrations.generic.sparql"
        )
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    if result_set.is_boolean and result_set.error:
        raise _incomplete(result_set.error, result_set)
    return result_set

def __init__(self, allowed: int, position: str) -> None:
    # Which types of terms the column allows (bits 1 << KIND_*), and its name
    # in error messages
    self.allowed = allowed
    self.position = position
    # The current run: its term, and how many cells it has. A run of the
    # default graph is a run of unbound cells
    self.run_term: object = None
    self.run_length = 0
    self.run_unbound = False
    # Run values that took one cell each since the last layout token
    self.skip = 0
    self.layouts: list[int] = []
    self.value_count = 0
    # The types of the run values (bits 1 << KIND_*), and once there is more
    # than one, the type of each value, packed as written: 2 bits each, four
    # in a byte, from the lowest bits
    self.kinds_used = 0
    self.kinds: list[int] | None = None
    # IRIs: name indices (0 if the previous one + 1) and prefix indices (0 if
    # the same as the previous one). If all prefix indices are the same, the
    # first is written alone.
    self.name_ids: list[int] = []
    self.prefix_ids: list[int] = []
    self.last_name_id = 0
    self.last_prefix_id = -1
    self.prefix_ids_differ = False
    # Literals: lexical forms and literal kinds, and the language tags they
    # refer to, with their base directions. If all literal kinds are the same,
    # the first is written alone.
    self.lex_values: list[str] = []
    self.literal_kinds: list[int] = []
    self.last_literal_kind = -1
    self.literal_kinds_differ = False
    self.langtags: list[str] = []
    self.langtag_directions: list[int] = []
    # Index of each language tag in langtags, one dict per base direction
    self.langtag_indices: list[dict[str, int]] = [{}, {}, {}]
    self.bnodes: list[str] = []
    self.triple_terms: list[jelly.RdfTripleTerm] = []

def add_value(self, term: EncodedTerm) -> None:
    """Add a run value: a term that is not the same as the one before."""
    kind = _kind_of(term)
    bit = 1 << kind
    used = self.kinds_used
    if used != bit:
        if not used & bit:
            self._new_kind(kind, used)
        kinds = self.kinds
        if kinds is not None:
            shift = (self.value_count & 3) << 1
            if shift:
                kinds[-1] |= kind << shift
            else:
                kinds.append(kind)
    self.value_count += 1
    if kind == KIND_IRI:
        self._add_iri(term.first, term.second)
    elif kind == KIND_LITERAL:
        self._add_literal(term)
    elif kind == KIND_BNODE:
        self.bnodes.append(term.text)
    else:
        assert term.triple_term is not None
        self.triple_terms.append(term.triple_term)

def end_run(self) -> None:
    """End the current run, adding a layout token if it isn't one cell long."""
    length = self.run_length
    if not length:
        return
    if self.run_unbound:
        self._token(TOKEN_UNBOUND, length - 1)
        self.run_unbound = False
    elif length > 1:
        self._token(0, length - 2)
    else:
        self.skip += 1
    self.run_length = 0

def write(self, column: jelly.RdfColumn) -> None:
    """Write the column into its message, and empty it for the next frame."""
    if self.run_unbound:
        # Unbound cells at the end are skipped: the parser pads the column
        self.run_length = 0
        self.run_unbound = False
    else:
        self.end_run()
    if self.layouts:
        column.layouts.extend(self.layouts)
    if self.name_ids:
        self._write_iris(column)
    if self.lex_values:
        self._write_literals(column)
    if self.bnodes:
        column.bnodes.extend(self.bnodes)
    if self.triple_terms:
        column.triple_terms.extend(self.triple_terms)
    if self.kinds is not None:
        column.kinds = bytes(self.kinds)
    self.clear()

def add(self, column: Column, term: object) -> None:
    """Add a subject, predicate or object to its column."""
    if column.run_length and self.encoder.same_term(column.run_term, term):
        column.run_length += 1
        return
    column.end_run()
    encoded = self.encoded
    self.encoder.encode_spo(term, encoded)
    column.add_value(encoded)
    column.run_term = term
    column.run_length = 1
    if encoded.triple_term is not None:

def add_graph(self, term: object) -> None:
    """Add a graph name, an unbound cell for the default graph."""
    column = self.graphs
    assert column is not None
    if column.run_length and self.encoder.same_term(column.run_term, term):
        column.run_length += 1
        return
    encoded = self.encoded
    self.encoder.encode_graph(term, encoded)
    if encoded.kind == TERM_DEFAULT_GRAPH:
        if not column.run_unbound:
            column.end_run()
            column.run_unbound = True
    else:
        column.end_run()
        column.add_value(encoded)
    column.run_term = term
    column.run_length += 1

def add_triple(
    self, terms: Iterable[object], repeated_terms: list[object | None]
) -> None:
    """Add a triple, and keep its terms in `repeated_terms`, as the row layout."""
    # Indexing a tuple is cheaper than unpacking any iterable
    if isinstance(terms, tuple) and len(terms) == _TRIPLE_SIZE:
        s = terms[0]
        p = terms[1]
        o = terms[2]
    else:
        s, p, o = terms
    self.add(self.subjects, s)
    self.add(self.predicates, p)
    self.add(self.objects, o)
    repeated_terms[0] = s
    repeated_terms[1] = p
    repeated_terms[2] = o
    self.row_count += 1

def add_namespace(self, name: str, iri: str) -> None:
    """Add a namespace declaration, which comes before the frame's statements."""
    prefix_index, name_index = self.encoder.iri_indices(iri)
    # The IRIs of the declarations are a sequence of their own
    written_prefix = (
        0 if prefix_index == self.namespace_prefix_index else prefix_index
    )
    written_name = 0 if name_index == self.namespace_name_index + 1 else name_index
    self.namespace_prefix_index = prefix_index
    self.namespace_name_index = name_index
    self.namespaces.append((name, written_prefix, written_name))

def write(self, batch: jelly.RdfColumnBatch) -> None:
    """Write the frame's statements into its batch, and start the next frame."""
    encoder = self.encoder
    batch.row_count = self.row_count
    encoder.names.packed.write(batch.names)
    encoder.prefixes.packed.write(batch.prefixes)
    encoder.datatypes.packed.write(batch.datatypes)
    for name, prefix_index, name_index in self.namespaces:
        declaration = batch.namespaces.add()
        declaration.name = name
        declaration.value.prefix_id = prefix_index
        declaration.value.name_id = name_index
    if self.row_count:
        self.subjects.write(batch.subjects)
        self.predicates.write(batch.predicates)
        self.objects.write(batch.objects)
        graphs = self.graphs
        if graphs is not None:
            if graphs.value_count:
                graphs.write(batch.graphs)
            else:
                # All statements are in the default graph: no column at all
                graphs.clear()
    if self.message_lengths:
        batch.message_lengths.extend(self.message_lengths)
    self.row_count = 0
    self.rows_in_messages = 0
    self.message_lengths = []
    self.namespaces = []
    self.new_frame()

A term encoded for a statement, before it is written into the statement.

A statement is written in two steps: first its terms are encoded (adding new lookup entries to the frame), then the terms are written into the statement's row (row layout) or columns (column layout). This way the row is filled in place, and never copied.

def __init__(
    self,
    lookup_preset: options.LookupPreset | None = None,
) -> None:
    if lookup_preset is None:
        lookup_preset = options.LookupPreset()
    self.lookup_preset = lookup_preset
    self.names = LookupEncoder(lookup_size=lookup_preset.max_names)
    self.prefixes = LookupEncoder(lookup_size=lookup_preset.max_prefixes)
    self.datatypes = LookupEncoder(lookup_size=lookup_preset.max_datatypes)
    # Where rows for new lookup entries go in the row layout. A stream replaces
    # it with its own.
    self.flow: FrameFlow = ManualFrameFlow()
    self.iri_cache: dict[str, _CachedIri] = {}
    # Cleared when full, so that a long stream doesn't grow it without bound
    self.iri_cache_size = max(4 * lookup_preset.max_names, 1024)
    # The encoded subject, predicate, object and graph of the statement
    self.encoded = [EncodedTerm() for _ in range(4)]
    # Set by streams of Jelly-RDF 1.2. Then IRIs are encoded with the indices of
    # their entries, new entries are packed (see PackedEntries), and quoted
    # triples are encoded as triple terms.
    self.column_layout = False
    # The RDF version that a Jelly-RDF 1.2 stream declares, which limits its terms
    self.rdf_version: int = jelly.RDF_VERSION_UNSPECIFIED
    # The IRI sequence of the triple terms of a frame (only the object column can
    # have them): the indices of the last IRI. -1 makes the first IRI state its
    # prefix.
    self.triple_prefix_index = -1
    self.triple_name_index = 0
    # How deep the triple term being encoded is nested, and how many IRIs the
    # outermost one has so far
    self.triple_depth = 0
    self.triple_iris = 0

def new_frame(self, iris: int, literals: int = 1) -> None:
    """
    Start encoding a new frame in the column layout.

    The frame is one epoch of the lookups: all its entries must fit in them,
    because they are all applied before its statements are read. So each lookup
    gets a budget, which leaves room for one more statement (see has_room()).

    Args:
        iris (int): the most IRIs that one statement can have.
        literals (int): maximum number of literals in one statement or row. In a
            statement, only the object can be a literal.

    """
    self.names.lookup.new_epoch(_budget(self.names, iris))
    self.prefixes.lookup.new_epoch(_budget(self.prefixes, iris))
    self.datatypes.lookup.new_epoch(_budget(self.datatypes, literals))
    self.triple_prefix_index = -1
    self.triple_name_index = 0

def iri_indices(self, iri_string: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """
    Return the indices of an IRI's prefix and name entries, adding new entries.

    Most IRIs repeat, so how an IRI splits into prefix and name, and the
    indices of their entries, are cached (see _CachedIri).

    Args:
        iri_string (str): full iri in string format.

    Returns:
        tuple[int, int]: indices in prefix and name tables.

    """
    cached = self.iri_cache.get(iri_string)
    if cached is None:
        if len(self.iri_cache) >= self.iri_cache_size:
            self.iri_cache.clear()
        if self.prefixes.lookup.max_size:
            prefix, name = split_iri(iri_string)
        else:
            prefix, name = "", iri_string
        cached = _CachedIri(prefix, name)
        self.iri_cache[iri_string] = cached

    prefix_index = 0
    prefixes = self.prefixes
    if prefixes.lookup.max_size:
        prefix_index = cached.prefix_index
        if prefix_index and prefixes.lookup.keys[prefix_index] is cached.prefix:
            prefixes.lookup.touch(prefix_index)
        else:
            prefix_index = self._new_prefix_index(cached)

    names = self.names
    name_index = cached.name_index
    if name_index and names.lookup.keys[name_index] is cached.name:
        names.lookup.touch(name_index)
    else:
        name_index = self._new_name_index(cached)
    return prefix_index, name_index

def encode_iri_indices(self, iri_string: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """
    Encode lookup indices for IRI, as written in the row layout.

    The indices are relative to the IRI before (see RdfIri), so IRIs must be
    encoded in the order they are written.

    Args:
        iri_string (str): full iri in string format.

    Returns:
        tuple[int, int]: indices in prefix and name tables.

    """
    prefix_index, name_index = self.iri_indices(iri_string)
    prefixes = self.prefixes
    if prefixes.lookup.max_size:
        prefix_index = prefixes.prefix_index_to_write(
            prefix_index, empty=not prefixes.lookup.keys[prefix_index]
        )
    return prefix_index, self.names.name_index_to_write(name_index)

def encode_literal(
    self,
    *,
    lex: str,
    language: str | None = None,
    datatype: str | None = None,
    direction: str | None = None,
    out: EncodedTerm,
) -> None:
    """
    Encode literal into `out`, adding a new datatype entry.

    Args:
        lex (str): lexical form/literal value
        language (str | None, optional): langtag. Defaults to None.
        datatype (str | None, optional): data type if
        it is a typed literal. Defaults to None.
        direction (str | None, optional): base direction of a language-tagged
            string, "ltr" or "rtl". Defaults to None.
        out (EncodedTerm): where to put the encoded literal.

    Raises:
        JellyConformanceError: if datatype specified while
            datatable is not used, or if the stream can't have the base
            direction.

    """
    datatype_index = 0
    direction_value = 0
    if language:
        if direction:
            direction_value = self.encode_direction(direction)
    elif datatype and datatype != options.STRING_DATATYPE_IRI:
        datatype_index = self.encode_datatype(datatype)
    out.kind = TERM_LITERAL
    out.text = lex
    out.lang = language or ""
    out.first = datatype_index
    out.direction = direction_value

def encode_direction(self, direction: str) -> int:
    """Return the RdfBaseDirection value of a base direction."""
    value = _DIRECTIONS.get(direction, 0)
    if not value:
        msg = f"unknown base direction: {direction!r}, expected 'ltr' or 'rtl'"
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    if not self.column_layout:
        msg = (
            "literals with a base direction can only be written in Jelly-RDF 1.2 "
            "(protocol version 3)"
        )
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    if self.rdf_version == jelly.RDF_VERSION_1_1:
        msg = "the stream declares RDF 1.1, which has no base directions"
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    return value

def encode_datatype(self, datatype: str) -> int:
    """Return the index of a datatype, adding an entry if it's new."""
    datatypes = self.datatypes
    if datatypes.lookup.max_size == 0:
        msg = (
            f"can't encode literal with type {datatype}: "
            "datatype lookup cannot be used if disabled "
            "(its size was set to 0)"
        )
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    index, set_index = datatypes.encode_entry(datatype)
    if set_index >= 0:
        if not self.column_layout:
            entry = self.flow.new_row().datatype
            entry.id = set_index
            entry.value = datatype
        elif datatype in (
            options.LANG_STRING_DATATYPE_IRI,
            options.DIR_LANG_STRING_DATATYPE_IRI,
        ):
            msg = f"a literal with the datatype {datatype} must have a language tag"
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        else:
            datatypes.packed.add(index, datatype)
    return index

def encode_quoted_triple(self, terms: Iterable[object], out: EncodedTerm) -> None:
    """
    Encode a quoted triple into `out`, adding new lookup entries.

    In the column layout, it is a triple term, see encode_triple_term().

    Notes:
        Although a triple, it is treated as a part of a statement.
        Repeated terms are not used when encoding quoted triples.

    Args:
        terms (Iterable[object]): triple terms to encode.
        out (EncodedTerm): where to put the encoded triple.

    """
    if self.column_layout:
        out.triple_term = self.encode_triple_term(terms)
        out.kind = TERM_TRIPLE
        return
    terms = iter(terms)
    triple = jelly.RdfTriple()
    for slot in range(3):
        term = EncodedTerm()
        self.encode_spo(next(terms), term)
        write_term(term, triple, slot)
    out.kind = TERM_TRIPLE
    out.triple = triple

def encode_triple_term(self, terms: Iterable[object]) -> jelly.RdfTripleTerm:
    """
    Encode a triple term of the column layout, adding new lookup entries.

    Its IRIs are in the IRI sequence of the frame's triple terms, in the order
    subject, predicate, object. `triple_iris` counts the IRIs of the outermost
    triple term, nested ones included.

    Args:
        terms (Iterable[object]): the subject, predicate and object.

    Returns:
        jelly.RdfTripleTerm: the triple term.

    """
    depth = self.triple_depth
    if not depth:
        rdf_version = self.rdf_version
        if rdf_version in (jelly.RDF_VERSION_1_1, jelly.RDF_VERSION_1_2_BASIC):
            name = (
                "RDF 1.1"
                if rdf_version == jelly.RDF_VERSION_1_1
                else "RDF 1.2 Basic"
            )
            msg = f"the stream declares {name}, which has no triple terms"
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        self.triple_iris = 0
    elif depth >= MAX_TRIPLE_TERM_DEPTH:
        msg = (
            f"triple terms nested deeper than {MAX_TRIPLE_TERM_DEPTH} levels "
            "are not supported"
        )
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    self.triple_depth = depth + 1
    try:
        triple = jelly.RdfTripleTerm()
        terms = iter(terms)
        term = EncodedTerm()
        self.encode_spo(next(terms), term)
        if term.kind == TERM_IRI:
            self._triple_term_iri(term, triple.s_iri)
        elif term.kind == TERM_BNODE:
            triple.s_bnode = term.text
        else:
            msg = "the subject of a triple term must be an IRI or a blank node"
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        self.encode_spo(next(terms), term)
        if term.kind != TERM_IRI:
            msg = "the predicate of a triple term must be an IRI"
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        self._triple_term_iri(term, triple.p_iri)
        self.encode_spo(next(terms), term)
        if term.kind == TERM_IRI:
            self._triple_term_iri(term, triple.o_iri)
        elif term.kind == TERM_BNODE:
            triple.o_bnode = term.text
        elif term.kind == TERM_LITERAL:
            _write_literal(term, triple.o_literal)
        else:
            assert term.triple_term is not None
            triple.o_triple_term.CopyFrom(term.triple_term)
    finally:
        self.triple_depth = depth
    return triple

def split_iri(iri_string: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """
    Split iri into prefix and name.

    Args:
        iri_string (str): full iri string.

    Returns:
        tuple[str, str]: iri's prefix and name.

    """
    # After the last "#", or else the last "/". Without either, all is the name.
    i = iri_string.rfind("#")
    if i < 0:
        i = iri_string.rfind("/")
    return iri_string[: i + 1], iri_string[i + 1 :]

def write_term(term: EncodedTerm, statement: Statement, slot: int) -> None:
    """Write an encoded subject (slot 0), predicate (1) or object (2)."""
    kind = term.kind
    if kind == TERM_IRI:
        iri = _iri_field(statement, slot)
        iri.prefix_id = term.first
        iri.name_id = term.second
    elif kind == TERM_LITERAL:
        _write_literal(term, _literal_field(statement, slot))
    elif kind == TERM_BNODE:
        _set_bnode(statement, slot, term.text)
    elif kind == TERM_TRIPLE:
        assert term.triple is not None
        _triple_field(statement, slot).CopyFrom(term.triple)

def encode_triple(
    terms: Iterable[object],
    term_encoder: TermEncoder,
    repeated_terms: list[object | None],
) -> None:
    """
    Encode one triple, adding its rows to the encoder's flow.

    Args:
        terms (Iterable[object]): original terms to encode
        term_encoder (TermEncoder): current encoder with lookup tables
        repeated_terms (list[object | None]): list of repeated terms.

    """
    term_encoder.new_epoch()
    encoded = term_encoder.encoded
    terms = iter(terms)
    # First encode the terms that changed, which adds rows for new lookup
    # entries, then add the triple's row after them and write the terms
    changed = 0
    for slot in range(3):
        term = next(terms)
        if not term_encoder.same_term(repeated_terms[slot], term):
            term_encoder.encode_spo(term, encoded[slot])
            repeated_terms[slot] = term
            changed |= 1 << slot
    triple = term_encoder.flow.new_row().triple
    if not changed:
        # Every term is repeated: the row is an empty triple
        triple.SetInParent()
    for slot in range(3):
        if changed & (1 << slot):
            write_term(encoded[slot], triple, slot)

def encode_quad(
    terms: Iterable[object],
    term_encoder: TermEncoder,
    repeated_terms: list[object | None],
) -> None:
    """
    Encode one quad, adding its rows to the encoder's flow.

    Args:
        terms (Iterable[object]): original terms to encode
        term_encoder (TermEncoder): current encoder with lookup tables
        repeated_terms (list[object | None]): list of repeated terms.

    """
    term_encoder.new_epoch()
    encoded = term_encoder.encoded
    terms = iter(terms)
    # See encode_triple()
    changed = 0
    for slot in range(3):
        term = next(terms)
        if not term_encoder.same_term(repeated_terms[slot], term):
            term_encoder.encode_spo(term, encoded[slot])
            repeated_terms[slot] = term
            changed |= 1 << slot
    g = next(terms)
    if not term_encoder.same_term(repeated_terms[3], g):
        term_encoder.encode_graph(g, encoded[3])
        repeated_terms[3] = g
        changed |= 1 << 3
    quad = term_encoder.flow.new_row().quad
    if not changed:
        quad.SetInParent()
    for slot in range(3):
        if changed & (1 << slot):
            write_term(encoded[slot], quad, slot)
    if changed & (1 << 3):
        write_graph(encoded[3], quad)

docs.title: FrameFlow(*, logical_type=None)
docs.text:
Abstract base class for producing Jelly frames from RDF stream rows.

Rows are added straight into the frame being built (see new_row()), so they never have to be copied: protobuf copies a message by serializing it and parsing it again.

In Jelly-RDF 1.2 streams, the frame's statements are in its column batch (see batch), and the rows only store the stream options. A frame may then also end because the lookups are full.

Allows for passing LogicalStreamType, required for logical subtypes and non-delimited streams.

def to_stream_frame(self) -> jelly.RdfStreamFrame | None:
    """
    Return the current frame, and start a new one.

    Returns:
        jelly.RdfStreamFrame | None: stream frame, None if it is empty

    """
    batch = self.batch
    if batch is not None and batch.has_content():
        batch.write(self.frame.columns)
    elif not len(self.rows):
        return None
    frame = self.frame
    self.frame = jelly.RdfStreamFrame()
    self.rows = self.frame.rows
    return frame

def frame_from_bounds(self) -> jelly.RdfStreamFrame | None:
    """
    Emit frame from flow if full.

    Returns:
        jelly.RdfStreamFrame | None: stream frame

    """
    batch = self.batch
    if batch is None:
        if len(self.rows) >= self.frame_size:
            return self.to_stream_frame()
    elif batch.row_count >= self.frame_size or not batch.has_room():
        return self.to_stream_frame()
    return None

def flow_for_type(logical_type: jelly.LogicalStreamType) -> type[FrameFlow]:
    """
    Return flow based on logical type requested.

    Note: uses base logical type for subtypes (i.e., SUBJECT_GRAPHS uses
        the same flow as its base type GRAPHS).

    Args:
        logical_type (jelly.LogicalStreamType): logical type requested.

    Raises:
        NotImplementedError: if (base) logical stream type is not supported.

    Returns:
        type[FrameFlow]: FrameFlow for respective logical type.

    """
    try:
        base_logical_type_value = logical_type % 10
        base_name = jelly.LogicalStreamType.Name(base_logical_type_value)
        return FLOW_DISPATCH[getattr(jelly.LogicalStreamType, base_name)]
    except KeyError:
        msg = (
            "unsupported logical stream type: "
            f"{jelly.LogicalStreamType.Name(logical_type)}"
        )
        raise NotImplementedError(msg) from None

def varint(value: int) -> bytes:
    r"""
    Encode a non-negative integer as a protobuf varint.

    >>> varint(300)
    b'\xac\x02'
    """
    out = bytearray()
    while value > _VARINT_PAYLOAD:
        out.append((value & _VARINT_PAYLOAD) | _VARINT_CONTINUATION)
        value >>= 7
    out.append(value)
    return bytes(out)

def write_delimited(frame: Message, output_stream: IO[bytes]) -> None:
    """Write a frame prefixed with its size (the delimited variant of Jelly)."""
    # protobuf's serialize_length_prefixed() needs write() to return the number of
    # bytes written, which not every stream does (e.g., rdflib's result streams)
    data = frame.SerializeToString()
    output_stream.write(varint(len(data)))
    output_stream.write(data)

docs.title: Lookup(max_size)
docs.text:
Fixed-size 1-based string-to-index mapping.

  • Assigns incrementing indices starting from 1.
  • When full, evicts entries in index order, skipping those used recently. This way new entries mostly take the previous index + 1, which Jelly writes as 0, making files smaller. The same strategy as in Jelly-JVM.
  • Index 0 is reserved for delta encoding in Jelly streams.

An entry is cold if it was not used in the last max_size // 2 uses. An entry is pinned if it was used in the current epoch (see new_epoch()): what is being encoded still refers to it, so it must not be evicted.

An epoch may have a budget: how many entries it may use. remaining counts down for every entry the epoch uses for the first time, and is negative once the epoch went over its budget.

Parameters:

Maximum number of entries. Zero disables lookup.

def __init__(self, max_size: int) -> None:
    self.data: dict[str, int] = {}
    self.max_size = max_size
    # By index, starting with an unused index 0: the key, and when the entry
    # was last used or added, counted in uses of this lookup (`now`)
    self.keys: list[str] = [""]
    self.last_use: list[int] = [0]
    self.now = 0
    self.epoch_start = _NO_EPOCH
    self.remaining = NO_BUDGET
    self.cold_age = max_size >> 1
    # The index of the last entry that replaced an evicted one, 0 if none yet
    self.last_evicted = 0

def touch(self, index: int) -> None:
    """Mark the entry at the index as used."""
    last_use = self.last_use
    if last_use[index] <= self.epoch_start:
        self.remaining -= 1
    self.now += 1
    last_use[index] = self.now

def use(self, key: str) -> int:
    """Mark the entry as used, and return its index, or 0 if there is none."""
    index = self.data.get(key, 0)
    if index:
        last_use = self.last_use
        if last_use[index] <= self.epoch_start:
            self.remaining -= 1
        self.now += 1
        last_use[index] = self.now
    return index

That is the next index in order (after the last evicted one), if it is cold and not pinned. Else, the least recently used one that is not pinned among a few indices spread evenly over the table, starting with that next index. The next eviction then goes on from the index picked, which is usually among a run of other old entries.

def victim(self) -> int:
    """
    Return the index of the entry to evict from the full lookup.

    That is the next index in order (after the last evicted one), if it is cold
    and not pinned. Else, the least recently used one that is not pinned among
    a few indices spread evenly over the table, starting with that next index.
    The next eviction then goes on from the index picked, which is usually
    among a run of other old entries.
    """
    size = self.max_size
    last_use = self.last_use
    epoch_start = self.epoch_start
    index = self.last_evicted + 1 if 1 <= self.last_evicted < size else 1
    last = last_use[index]
    if self.now - last >= self.cold_age and last <= epoch_start:
        return index
    best = 0
    best_last = _NO_EPOCH
    step = max(1, size // _SAMPLES)
    for _ in range(min(_SAMPLES, size)):
        last = last_use[index]
        if last < best_last and last <= epoch_start:
            best = index
            best_last = last
        index += step
        if index > size:
            index -= size
    if best:
        return best
    # The epoch pins every index sampled: the first index that it does not pin
    for _ in range(size):
        if last_use[index] <= epoch_start:
            return index
        index = 1 if index == size else index + 1
    msg = (
        f"a lookup of size {size} is too small to encode a single statement or "
        "row of results: it uses every one of its entries"
    )
    raise JellyConformanceError(msg)

def encode_entry_index(self, key: str) -> int | None:
    """
    Get or assign the index to use in an entry, and mark the entry as used.

    Call it once for every use of the key, before encode_*_term_index().

    Returns
    -------
    int or None
        - 0 if the new index is sequential (`last_assigned_index + 1`)
        - actual assigned/reused index otherwise
        - None if the key already exists

    If the return value is None, the entry is already in the lookup and does not
    need to be emitted. Any integer value (including 0) means the entry is new
    and should be emitted.

    """
    _, set_index = self.encode_entry(key)
    return None if set_index < 0 else set_index

def encode_entry(self, key: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """
    Get or add the entry for the key, and mark it as used.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[int, int]
        The entry's index, and the index to write in a new entry row: -1 if
        the entry was already there (no row needed), 0 if the new index is
        sequential (`last_assigned_index + 1`), else the index.

    """
    index = self.lookup.use(key)
    if index:
        return index, -1
    previous_index = self.last_assigned_index
    index = self.lookup.insert(key)
    self.last_assigned_index = index
    if index == previous_index + 1:
        return index, 0
    return index, index

def name_index_to_write(self, index: int) -> int:
    """Return how to write a reference to the name entry at the index."""
    previous_index = self.last_reused_index

def prefix_index_to_write(self, index: int, *, empty: bool) -> int:
    """Return how to write a reference to the prefix entry at the index."""
    previous_index = self.last_reused_index
    if empty and previous_index == 0:

    if previous_index == 0:
        return index
    if index == previous_index:
        return 0
    return index

def __init__(
    self, encoder: TermEncoder, options: SparqlOptions | None = None
) -> None:
    if options is None:
        options = SparqlOptions()
    if encoder.lookup_preset != options.lookup_preset:
        msg = "the encoder must have the lookup sizes of the options"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    self.encoder = encoder
    self.options = options
    encoder.column_layout = True
    encoder.rdf_version = options.rdf_version
    self.encoded = EncodedTerm()
    #: Variables of the current result set, None between result sets
    self.variables: list[str] | None = None
    self.columns: list[VariableColumn] = []
    # Reused buffer for the values of a binding, see binding()
    self.values: list[object | None] = []
    self.row_count = 0
    self.rows_per_frame = 1
    # Set when the single frame of a non-delimited stream is full
    self.full = False
    self.links: list[str] = []
    # Whether the stream options and the header still have to be written
    self.options_pending = True
    self.header_pending = False
    # `ended`: the single result set of a FLAT stream is done. `failed`: a row
    # failed to encode. Either way, nothing more can be written.
    self.ended = False
    self.failed = False
    # Column whose triple-term IRI state the encoder currently holds
    self.triple_owner: VariableColumn | None = None

def start(self, variables: Iterable[str], links: Sequence[str] = ()) -> None:
    """
    Start a solution sequence.

    Args:
        variables (Iterable[str]): variable names, in projection order. A
            leading "?" or "$" is removed.
        links (Sequence[str]): link IRIs for the result set, as in head.link of
            SPARQL JSON results.

    """
    self._check_can_start()
    names = variable_names(variables)
    self.variables = names
    self.columns = [VariableColumn() for _ in names]
    self.values = [None] * len(names)
    self.rows_per_frame = (
        min(self.options.rows_per_frame(len(names)), MAX_ROWS)
        if self.options.delimited
        else MAX_ROWS
    )
    self.header_pending = True
    self.links = list(links)
    self.new_frame()

def row(self, values: Sequence[object | None]) -> jelly.SparqlResultsFrame | None:
    """
    Add a row (solution) to the result set.

    Args:
        values (Sequence[object | None]): one value per variable, None if the
            variable is unbound.

    Returns:
        jelly.SparqlResultsFrame | None: the frame, if this row filled it.

    """
    columns = self.columns
    count = len(values)
    self._check_row(count)
    try:
        # mypyc indexes a typed tuple or list directly. Any other sequence goes
        # through the generic item lookup with a boxed int, which is slow.
        if type(values) is tuple:
            row_tuple: tuple[object | None, ...] = values
            for i in range(count):
                self.add(columns[i], row_tuple[i])
        elif type(values) is list:
            row_list: list[object | None] = values
            for i in range(count):
                self.add(columns[i], row_list[i])
        else:
            for i in range(count):
                self.add(columns[i], values[i])
    except BaseException:
        # The frame is half-written and can't be finished
        self.failed = True
        raise
    self.row_count += 1
    # End the frame as soon as it's full, rather than at the start of the next
    # row, so that a failing next row can't lose it
    if self.row_count >= self.rows_per_frame or not self.encoder.has_room():
        if self.options.delimited:
            return self.end_frame()
        self.full = True
    return None

def binding(
    self, binding: Mapping[Any, object | None], variables: Sequence[object]
) -> jelly.SparqlResultsFrame | None:
    """
    Add a row (solution) given as a mapping from variables to values.

    Args:
        binding (Mapping[Any, object | None]): values of the bound variables,
            keyed by variable or by variable name.
        variables (Sequence[object]): variables of the result set, in order.

    Returns:
        jelly.SparqlResultsFrame | None: the frame, if this row filled it.

    """
    values = self.values
    if len(variables) != len(values):
        msg = f"expected {len(values)} variables, got {len(variables)}"
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    # A typed list is cheaper to index, see row()
    keys: list[object] = variables if type(variables) is list else list(variables)
    bound = 0
    if type(binding) is dict:
        # Same loop, but with direct dict calls instead of method lookups
        mapping: dict[Any, object | None] = binding
        for i in range(len(values)):
            value = mapping.get(keys[i])
            values[i] = value
            if value is not None:
                bound += 1
    else:
        for i in range(len(values)):
            value = binding.get(keys[i])
            values[i] = value
            if value is not None:
                bound += 1
    if bound != len(binding):
        # Some keys are not the variable objects themselves (rdflib's
        # Variable("x") does not equal "x"), so look the values up by name
        by_name = {str(key): value for key, value in binding.items()}
        for i in range(len(values)):
            values[i] = by_name.get(str(variables[i]))
    return self.row(values)

def add(self, column: VariableColumn, term: object | None) -> None:
    """Add a value to a column. None is an unbound cell."""
    if term is None:
        if not column.run_unbound:
            column.end_run()
            column.run_unbound = True
        column.run_length += 1
        return
    if (
        column.run_length
        and not column.run_unbound
        and self.encoder.same_term(column.run_term, term)
    ):
        column.run_length += 1
        return
    column.end_run()
    if self.triple_owner is not None and self.triple_owner is not column:
        self._switch_triple_iris(column)
    encoded = self.encoded
    self.encoder.encode_spo(term, encoded)
    column.add_value(encoded)
    column.run_term = term
    column.run_length = 1
    if encoded.triple_term is not None:
        self._triple_term_added(column)

def write_frame(self, frame: jelly.SparqlResultsFrame) -> None:
    """Fill in the frame: options, header, lookup entries and rows."""
    self.write_start(frame)
    encoder = self.encoder
    row_count = self.row_count
    frame.row_count = row_count
    encoder.names.packed.write(frame.names)
    encoder.prefixes.packed.write(frame.prefixes)
    encoder.datatypes.packed.write(frame.datatypes)
    # Columns are left out of a frame with no rows
    if row_count:
        for column in self.columns:
            column.write(frame.columns.add())
    self.new_frame()

def write_start(self, frame: jelly.SparqlResultsFrame) -> None:
    """Add the stream options and the header, if they are still due."""
    if self.options_pending:
        frame.options.CopyFrom(self.stream_options())
        self.options_pending = False
    if self.header_pending:
        assert self.variables is not None
        frame.variables.extend(self.variables)
        self.header_pending = False
        if self.links:

def end(self, error: str = "") -> jelly.SparqlResultsFrame:
    """
    End the result set and return its last frame, which has the trailer.

    Args:
        error (str): reason the result set is incomplete, if it is. It tells
            readers that some results are missing.

    Returns:
        jelly.SparqlResultsFrame: the last frame.

    """
    frame = jelly.SparqlResultsFrame()
    if self.failed:
        if not error or self.variables is None:
            raise _failed()
        # Drop the frame's rows and their lookup entries. The lookups are then
        # out of sync with the reader, so the stream must end here.
        self.write_start(frame)
        self.ended = True
    elif self.variables is None:
        msg = "there is no result set to end, start one with start()"
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    else:
        self.write_frame(frame)
        if not self.options.punctuated:
            self.ended = True
    frame.trailer.SetInParent()
    frame.trailer.error = error
    self.variables = None
    return frame

    self,
    value: bool,  # noqa: FBT001
    links: Sequence[str] = (),

        error (str): reason the result is incomplete, if it is.

    if not self.options.punctuated:

    return frame

def links_value(links: Sequence[str]) -> bytes:
    r"""
    Join link IRIs with LF, for the "link" metadata key.

    >>> links_value(["http://example.org/a", "http://example.org/b"])
    b'http://example.org/a\nhttp://example.org/b'
    """
    for link in links:
        if "\n" in link:
            msg = f"a link cannot contain the LF character, as no IRI can: {link!r}"
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    return "\n".join(links).encode()

def variable_names(variables: Iterable[str]) -> list[str]:
    """
    Strip a leading "?" or "$" from each variable name.

    >>> variable_names(["?s", "$p", "o"])
    ['s', 'p', 'o']
    """
    names = []
    for variable in variables:
        name = str(variable)
        if name[:1] in ("?", "$"):
            name = name[1:]
        if not name:
            msg = "variable names cannot be empty"
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        names.append(name)
    return names

def error_message(error: BaseException) -> str:
    """
    Format an exception as the error message of a trailer.

    >>> error_message(KeyError("x"))
    "KeyError: 'x'"
    >>> error_message(JellyIncompleteResultsError("...", "timeout"))
    'timeout'
    """
    if isinstance(error, JellyIncompleteResultsError):
        # Passing on the error of a stream that was itself incomplete
        return error.error
    message = str(error)
    name = type(error).__name__
    return f"{name}: {message}" if message else name

def write_solutions(  # noqa: PLR0913 keyword-only options
    stream: SparqlStream,
    variables: Iterable[str],
    rows: Iterable[Sequence[object | None]],
    writer: FrameWriter,
    *,
    links: Sequence[str] = (),
    error: str = "",
) -> None:
    """
    Write a solution sequence (the result of a SELECT query) as one result set.

    If iterating the rows raises (e.g., the query fails midway), the result set is
    ended with that error so readers know it is incomplete, and the exception is
    re-raised. Pass `error` if the rows are already known to be incomplete.
    """
    stream.start(variables, links)
    try:
        for values in rows:
            frame = stream.row(values)
            if frame is not None:
                writer.write(frame)
    except Exception as failure:
        _end_with(stream, writer, failure)
        raise
    writer.write(stream.end(error))

        stream (SparqlStream): the stream.
        variables (Sequence[object]): the variables, as str objects (e.g., rdflib's
            Variable). Their names are written.
        bindings (Iterable[Mapping[Any, object | None]]): the rows, see
            SparqlStream.binding().
        writer (FrameWriter): writer of the frames.
        links (Sequence[str]): link IRIs for the results.
        error (str): reason the rows are incomplete, if known.

    """
    stream.start([str(variable) for variable in variables], links)
    try:
        for binding in bindings:
            frame = stream.binding(binding, variables)
            if frame is not None:
                writer.write(frame)
    except Exception as failure:
        _end_with(stream, writer, failure)
        raise
    writer.write(stream.end(error))

def column_batch(self, params: StreamParameters) -> ColumnBatch:
    """Set the stream up to write Jelly-RDF 1.2, and return its column batch."""
    max_names = self.options.lookup_preset.max_names
    if max_names < MIN_COLUMN_NAME_LOOKUP_SIZE:
        msg = (
            f"the name lookup size is {max_names}, but in Jelly-RDF 1.2 it must "
            f"be at least {MIN_COLUMN_NAME_LOOKUP_SIZE}"
        )
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    encoder = self.encoder
    encoder.column_layout = True
    encoder.rdf_version = params.rdf_version
    stream_type = stream_type_for(params, self.stream_types.logical_type)
    batch = ColumnBatch(
        encoder,
        quads=self.physical_type == jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_QUADS,
        messages=stream_type == jelly.RDF_STREAM_TYPE_MESSAGES,
    )
    self.flow.batch = batch
    return batch

def infer_flow(self) -> FrameFlow:
    """
    Return flow based on the stream options provided.

    Returns:
        FrameFlow: initialised FrameFlow object.

    """
    flow: FrameFlow
    if self.options.params.delimited:
        if self.options.logical_type != jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED:
            flow_class = flow_for_type(self.options.logical_type)
        else:
            flow_class = self.default_delimited_flow_class

        if issubclass(flow_class, BoundedFrameFlow) and (
            self.options.logical_type
            in (
                jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_FLAT_TRIPLES,
                jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_FLAT_QUADS,
            )
        ):
            flow = flow_class(
                logical_type=self.options.logical_type,
                frame_size=self.options.frame_size,
            )
        else:
            flow = flow_class(logical_type=self.options.logical_type)
    else:
        flow = ManualFrameFlow(logical_type=self.options.logical_type)
    return flow

def namespace_declaration(self, name: str, iri: str) -> jelly.RdfStreamFrame | None:

            to start a new one

            name=name, value=iri, term_encoder=self.encoder

        return None
    # In Jelly-RDF 1.2, the declarations of a frame come before its statements

        frame = self.flow.to_stream_frame()
    batch.add_namespace(name, iri)
    return frame

Encode the subject, predicate and object that were set since the last emit.

They are encoded in this order no matter in which order they were set: IRIs are encoded relative to the IRI before them, in the order the parser reads them. Rows for new lookup entries are added to the flow.

Returns: int: which of them were encoded, as bits 0 (subject) to 2 (object).

def encode_changed_spo(self) -> int:
    """
    Encode the subject, predicate and object that were set since the last emit.

    They are encoded in this order no matter in which order they were set:
    IRIs are encoded relative to the IRI before them, in the order the parser
    reads them. Rows for new lookup entries are added to the flow.

    Returns:
        int: which of them were encoded, as bits 0 (subject) to 2 (object).

    """
    terms = self.repeated_terms
    encoded = self.encoder.encoded
    changed = 0
    if self.subject_changed:
        self.encoder.encode_spo(terms[0], encoded[0])
        self.subject_changed = False
        changed = 1
    if self.predicate_changed:
        self.encoder.encode_spo(terms[1], encoded[1])
        self.predicate_changed = False
        changed |= 2
    if self.object_changed:
        self.encoder.encode_spo(terms[2], encoded[2])
        self.object_changed = False
        changed |= 4
    return changed

def add_changed_spo(self, batch: ColumnBatch) -> None:
    """Add the subject, predicate and object of the cursor API to their columns."""
    terms = self.repeated_terms
    batch.add_changed(batch.subjects, terms[0], changed=self.subject_changed)
    batch.add_changed(batch.predicates, terms[1], changed=self.predicate_changed)
    batch.add_changed(batch.objects, terms[2], changed=self.object_changed)
    self.subject_changed = False
    self.predicate_changed = False
    self.object_changed = False

def write_changed_spo(self, statement: Statement, changed: int) -> None:
    """Write the terms encoded by encode_changed_spo() into the statement."""
    encoded = self.encoder.encoded
    if not changed:
        # Every term is repeated: the row is an empty statement
        statement.SetInParent()
    if changed & 1:
        write_term(encoded[0], statement, 0)
    if changed & 2:
        write_term(encoded[1], statement, 1)
    if changed & 4:
        write_term(encoded[2], statement, 2)

@classmethod
def for_rdflib(cls, options: SerializerOptions | None = None) -> Stream:
    """
    Initialize stream with RDFLib encoder.

    Args:
        options (SerializerOptions | None, optional): Stream options.
            Defaults to None.

    Raises:
        TypeError: if Stream is passed, and not a Stream for specific physical type.

    Returns:
        Stream: initialized stream with RDFLib encoder.

    """
    if cls is Stream:
        msg = "Stream is an abstract base class, use a subclass instead"
        raise TypeError(msg)
    from pyjelly.integrations.rdflib.encode import (  # noqa: PLC0415
        RDFLibTermEncoder,
    )

    lookup_preset: LookupPreset | None = None
    if options is not None:
        lookup_preset = options.lookup_preset
    return cls(
        encoder=RDFLibTermEncoder(lookup_preset=lookup_preset),
        options=options,
    )

def triple(self, terms: Iterable[object]) -> jelly.RdfStreamFrame | None:
    """
    Process one triple to Protobuf messages.

    Note:
        Adds new rows to the current flow and returns StreamFrame if
        frame size conditions are met.

    Returns:

            flow supports frames slicing and current flow is full

    if batch is None:

    Add a triple made of the terms set with the cursor API.

def emit(self) -> jelly.RdfStreamFrame | None:
    """
    Add a quad made of the terms set with the cursor API.

    Returns:
        jelly.RdfStreamFrame | None: stream frame if
            flow supports frames slicing and current flow is full

    """
    batch = self.batch
    if batch is not None:
        self.add_changed_spo(batch)
        batch.add_graph_changed(self.repeated_terms[3], changed=self.graph_changed)
        self.graph_changed = False
        batch.row_count += 1
        return self.flow.frame_from_bounds()
    self.encoder.new_epoch()
    # The terms first, as they add rows for new lookup entries. The graph
    # comes last, as in the parser.
    changed = self.encode_changed_spo()
    graph_changed = self.graph_changed
    if graph_changed:
        self.encoder.encode_graph(self.repeated_terms[3], self.encoder.encoded[3])
        self.graph_changed = False
        changed |= 8
    quad = self.flow.new_row().quad
    self.write_changed_spo(quad, changed)
    if graph_changed:
        write_graph(self.encoder.encoded[3], quad)
    return self.flow.frame_from_bounds()
